source_credit: Baltasar Gracián · Oráculo manual y arte de prudencia (1647), all 300 maxims, read in Joseph Jacobs' English translation 'The Art of Worldly Wisdom' (Macmillan, 1892; 1904 printing, archive.org item artofworldlywisd00gracuoft), public domain. Maxim titles are Jacobs'. Every text is our own distillation plus an application for Nour, not a quotation; no modern translation was used.

entries.text: TL;DR: Everything is at its Acme (maxim 1). Key points: The world has grown more complicated, so getting along in it now demands far more skill than it once did. Dealing well with even one person takes the care that used to be needed for a crowd. For Nour: a single walk-in today expects speed, honesty and a clear estimate all at once, so treat each counter conversation as a skill to practice, not a routine.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 1 'Everything is at its Acme' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Character and Intellect (maxim 2). Key points: Brains alone fall short; a person also needs character, and only the two together lead to a good life. Lacking either, people end up in the wrong role and the wrong company. For Nour: when judging a hire, weigh whether they keep their word as heavily as whether they can diagnose a car, because a sharp tech without integrity costs more than he earns.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 2 'Character and Intellect' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Keep Matters for a Time in Suspense (maxim 3). Key points: Gracián advises against revealing plans at once: some reserve heightens interest, while an announced plan invites criticism and doubles the embarrassment if it fails. For Nour: hold a new NOUR OS feature or shop change until it actually works before announcing it, but never use suspense on customers; an estimate should always be plain and complete.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 3 'Keep Matters for a Time in Suspense' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Knowledge and Courage (maxim 4). Key points: Greatness rests on knowing and daring together. Knowledge that never acts is barren, and nerve without knowledge is blind. For Nour: knowing how many estimates were declined is half the job; the other half is acting on it, such as changing how estimates are explained, instead of only watching the report.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 4 'Knowledge and Courage' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Create a Feeling of Dependence (maxim 5). Key points: Gracián says people who still need you treat you better than people who merely thank you, so he advises keeping others in need rather than fully satisfied, while warning not to let someone's trouble linger for your own gain. For Nour: earn dependence honestly, by being the shop customers trust to tell the truth about their car, never by holding back a fix or leaving a problem half solved to bring them back.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 5 'Create a Feeling of Dependence' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: A Man at his Highest Point (maxim 6). Key points: Nobody is born finished; people grow day by day in character and craft until they reach maturity, which shows in clear thinking, sound judgment and a steady will. Some never get there and some ripen late. For Nour: give the crew room to grow into bigger roles over time, and judge your own progress by the quality of your decisions, not by how busy the week was.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 6 'A Man at his Highest Point' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Avoid Victories over Superiors (maxim 7). Key points: Outshining those above you breeds resentment; people in power accept help but not being surpassed, so good advice should feel like a reminder rather than a correction. For Nour: you are the one above now, so watch for the reverse; when Mash or Manny has a better idea than yours, adopt it openly and give them the credit so they keep bringing ideas.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 7 'Avoid Victories over Superiors' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: To be without Passions (maxim 8). Key points: Ruling your own impulses is the highest form of command. A person pushed around by passing moods cannot be trusted with large responsibility, and self-mastery is the fastest road back to good standing. For Nour: when a customer yells at the counter or a supplier misses a delivery, decide what to do after the heat passes, not in the middle of it.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 8 'To be without Passions' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Avoid the Faults of your Nation (maxim 9). Key points: Everyone absorbs flaws from their surroundings: their country, family, trade and age. Correcting those inherited faults earns extra credit precisely because nobody expects it. For Nour: the repair trade is known for upselling and vague answers, so being the shop that explains every line of an estimate in plain words is how you stand apart.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 9 'Avoid the Faults of your Nation' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Fortune and Fame (maxim 10). Key points: Luck is fickle and serves you only while you live, while a good name is earned and outlasts you. Fortune can be helped along, but reputation has to be built. For Nour: a slow or busy week is fortune, the name of the shop on Euclid Ave is fame, so protect the name even on a day when cutting a corner would pay.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 10 'Fortune and Fame' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Cultivate those who can teach you (maxim 11). Key points: Make friendship a school: spend time with people who know more, so conversation brings both pleasure and instruction. The best circles teach by example as much as by talk. For Nour: seek out owners and builders who are further along, and ask them specific questions about how they run their counters, their crews or their software.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 11 'Cultivate those who can teach you' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Nature and Art (maxim 12). Key points: Natural talent is only raw material; training is the workmanship that finishes it. Without cultivation even the best gifts stay rough, and every excellence needs some polish. For Nour: a new hire with good hands still needs a routine for writing estimates and greeting walk-ins, because talent without that polish shows up as confused customers.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 12 'Nature and Art' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Act sometimes on Second Thoughts, sometimes on First Impulse (maxim 13). Key points: Gracián paints life as a contest of wits in which people feint and hide their real aims, and the sharp observer looks past the first appearance to catch the true move. For Nour: use this as a defense, not a tactic; when a vendor's first offer looks too good, wait for the second and third detail before signing, and keep your own dealings with customers straightforward.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 13 'Act sometimes on Second Thoughts, sometimes on First Impulse' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: The Thing Itself and the Way it is done (maxim 14). Key points: Substance is not enough; manner matters too. A poor delivery can spoil even a fair point, while a good one softens hard news and helps people through difficulty. For Nour: telling a walk-in their brakes are unsafe is the substance; saying it calmly, showing them the part and laying out their choices is the manner that keeps their trust.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 14 'The Thing Itself and the Way it is done' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Keep Ministering Spirits (maxim 15). Key points: Wise leaders surround themselves with capable advisers who work through hard questions for them, so that many minds speak through one voice; if you cannot employ such people, make them your friends. For Nour: this is part of what NOUR OS is for, gathering good thinking in one place, but also lean on Mash and Manny's knowledge of the floor before deciding shop operations alone.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 15 'Keep Ministering Spirits' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Knowledge and Good Intentions (maxim 16). Key points: Intelligence only lasts when it is joined to good will. A clever mind serving bad aims does more damage, and does it more subtly, than a dull one. For Nour: build NOUR OS features that use customer records to serve customers, such as reminders they would actually want, never tricks to squeeze extra work out of them.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 16 'Knowledge and Good Intentions' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Vary the Mode of Action (maxim 17). Key points: A rival who learns your pattern can anticipate and block you, so do not always act in the same predictable way. Even a pattern of second thoughts can be read in time. For Nour: be predictable to customers and the crew and unpredictable only to competitors; vary how you market the shop and test new channels instead of repeating one campaign until it goes stale.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 17 'Vary the Mode of Action' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Application and Ability (maxim 18). Key points: Eminence needs both talent and effort, and steady work carries an average person further than idle talent carries a gifted one. Whatever costs little is worth little. For Nour: the plain habit of reviewing counter invoices every week will beat occasional bursts of brilliant planning that never get followed through.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 18 'Application and Ability' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Arouse no Exaggerated Expectations on entering (maxim 19). Key points: Big advance billing sets you up to disappoint, because reality rarely matches what people imagine. Promise modestly and let the results exceed the hopes. For Nour: when telling a customer how long a job will take, give the honest time, and when launching anything new, describe what it does today rather than what it might someday do.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 19 'Arouse no Exaggerated Expectations on entering' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: A Man of the Age (maxim 20). Key points: Even exceptional people depend on their era; not everyone is born into a time that suits them, and even good qualities go in and out of fashion. The wise can wait for a better season. For Nour: this is a good moment for a small shop to run on its own software, so use the window while capable tools are within reach instead of waiting for a perfect time.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 20 'A Man of the Age' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: The Art of being Lucky (maxim 21). Key points: Luck follows rules, and the wise help it along with care; people who press forward boldly do better than those who wait passively at the door. For Nour: being open 7 days for walk-ins is a way of standing where luck can find you, since the shop catches the driver who needs help on a Sunday only because it chose to be there.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 21 'The Art of being Lucky' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: A Man of Knowledge to the Point (maxim 22). Key points: Useful knowledge is practical and current, an expert's grasp of what is actually going on, plus a stock of apt examples and sayings ready for the right moment. A well-timed remark can teach more than a lecture. For Nour: this wisdom pack is meant to be that stock, so ask Nick for the fitting principle when a real decision comes up rather than reading theory for its own sake.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 22 'A Man of Knowledge to the Point' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Be Spotless (maxim 23). Key points: Small flaws draw attention out of proportion to their size, and ill will keeps pointing at them. Fix the ones you can, and where you cannot, turn them into something people respect. For Nour: a messy waiting area or a mistyped invoice can overshadow excellent repair work, so clean up the small visible defects customers notice first.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 23 'Be Spotless' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Keep the Imagination under Control (maxim 24). Key points: Imagination can make life happy or miserable: it either magnifies the dangers of acting or sells fantasy rewards, and it needs disciplined correction. Left alone, it rules instead of serving. For Nour: when you picture worst cases about a slow week or best cases about a new feature, check the actual invoices and usage before acting on the story in your head.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 24 'Keep the Imagination under Control' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Know how to take a Hint (maxim 25). Key points: The things that matter most are often only half said, so learn to read what is implied. Be slow to believe good news and quick to take bad news seriously. For Nour: when a customer says they will think about an estimate, it may be a polite no, so ask what would help them decide instead of assuming they will be back.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 25 'Know how to take a Hint' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Find out each Man's Thumbscrew (maxim 26). Key points: Gracián teaches that everyone has a ruling motive, such as pride, profit or pleasure, and that knowing it gives you leverage over their will. For Nour: learn what each crew member actually cares about, whether more responsibility, steady hours or new skills, so you can motivate them fairly; never press on a customer's fear to sell work they do not need.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 26 'Find out each Man's Thumbscrew' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Prize Intensity more than Extent (maxim 27). Key points: Quality outweighs quantity. Spreading yourself across everything makes you ordinary everywhere, while depth in a few things produces real excellence. For Nour: a handful of NOUR OS features that work every day beat a long list of half-wired ones, so finish and harden what exists before adding more.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 27 'Prize Intensity more than Extent' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Common in Nothing (maxim 28). Key points: Do not take your taste or your judgment from the crowd. Popular applause is a poor measure, and the wise look past whatever dazzles the masses to see how it works. For Nour: do not copy what other shops do just because it is trending online; decide by what serves your customers and shows up in the invoices.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 28 'Common in Nothing' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: A Man of Rectitude (maxim 29). Key points: Real integrity holds to what is right under pressure from crowds, powerful people, friends or self-interest. Many praise it, but few keep it once it starts to cost them. For Nour: the test is the day honesty costs money, such as telling a customer a part still has life left when replacing it would bring in more.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 29 'A Man of Rectitude' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Have naught to do with Occupations of Ill-repute (maxim 30). Key points: Stay away from disreputable work and from fads that bring notoriety rather than respect. Chasing strangeness makes you known mainly as a joke. For Nour: avoid gimmicky stunts or questionable side deals that could tie the shop's name to something cheap, because steady respect is worth more than a burst of attention.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 30 'Have naught to do with Occupations of Ill-repute' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Select the Lucky and avoid the Unlucky (maxim 31). Key points: Misfortune usually follows poor judgment and spreads to those standing nearby. Do not let a small evil in, since bigger ones follow, and when unsure, follow people whose judgment has proven sound. For Nour: be careful with vendors or contacts who keep stumbling into trouble, because their pattern of bad calls tends to land on whoever is close to them.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 31 'Select the Lucky and avoid the Unlucky' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Have the Reputation of being Gracious (maxim 32). Key points: The best use of a strong position is the ability to do more good than others can. People who do kind things make friends, while those who withhold kindness out of bad temper make none. For Nour: as owner you can make a hard day easier for a customer whose car broke down far from home or a crew member dealing with a problem, and those acts build the shop's name more than ads.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 32 'Have the Reputation of being Gracious' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Know how to Withdraw (maxim 33). Key points: Beyond saying no to others, learn to say no to yourself: drop affairs that eat your time and are not really your concern, and do not overuse other people's help. For Nour: step back from tasks Mash and Manny can run so your hours go to decisions only you can make, and never lean on any one person beyond what they offer freely.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 33 'Know how to Withdraw' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Know your strongest Point (maxim 34). Key points: Find the quality where you naturally excel and develop it, and the rest will benefit. Most people fight their own nature and end up excellent at nothing. For Nour: notice whether your edge is building systems, reading people or making deals, then put more of your hours there and hand the rest to people who are stronger at it.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 34 'Know your strongest Point' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Think over Things, most over the most Important (maxim 35). Key points: Fools come to grief for lack of thought and weigh things on the wrong scale, fussing over trivia and skimming what matters. The wise think about everything, but most deeply where the stakes are highest. For Nour: spend little thought on the color of a button in NOUR OS and serious thought on anything touching customer data, money or the crew's livelihoods.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 35 'Think over Things, most over the most Important' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: In Acting or Refraining, weigh your Luck (maxim 36). Key points: Fortune runs in streaks nobody can predict, so learn to read which way it is running. Press forward while things go your way, and keep a low profile when they turn against you. For Nour: in a strong month, fund the improvement you have been postponing; in a rough stretch, hold off on big new commitments until the trend turns.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 36 'In Acting or Refraining, weigh your Luck' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Keep a Store of Sarcasms, and know how to use them (maxim 37). Key points: Barbed remarks can test someone's mood or quietly wreck a relationship, and one cutting word can break a bond that open hostility never could; expect such jabs so they miss. For Nour: avoid cutting jokes at the counter or toward the crew, since one careless jab can undo years of loyalty, and do not let other people's jabs knock you off course.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 37 'Keep a Store of Sarcasms, and know how to use them' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Leave your Luck while Winning (maxim 38). Key points: Good players quit while they are ahead, because a long run of luck grows riskier the higher it piles. A well-timed exit is worth as much as a bold attack. For Nour: when a promotion or marketing channel is working, plan its end before it fades, rather than riding it until the results collapse.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 38 'Leave your Luck while Winning' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Recognise when Things are ripe, and then enjoy them (maxim 39). Key points: Everything reaches a peak and then declines, and good taste knows the ripe moment, both for using a thing and for trading it. For Nour: ship a NOUR OS feature when it is solid enough to help rather than polishing it forever, and when the shop has a good week, take the time to notice it instead of rushing past.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 39 'Recognise when Things are ripe, and then enjoy them' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: The Goodwill of People (maxim 40). Key points: Admiration is good, but affection is better, and it is built mostly by practice: kind acts, fair words and better deeds, on top of whatever talent you have. For Nour: the crew's goodwill comes from things like fair schedules and being backed up in front of a difficult customer, not from speeches about teamwork.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 40 'The Goodwill of People' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Never Exaggerate (maxim 41). Key points: Superlatives either strain the truth or reveal poor judgment, and praise that outruns reality breeds a disappointment that turns on both the thing and the person who praised it. Exaggeration is a form of lying. For Nour: in shop marketing and in Nick's own reports, use measured words and real numbers, because overstated claims cost more credibility than they gain.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 41 'Never Exaggerate' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Born to Command (maxim 42). Key points: Some people lead by natural authority rather than by tricks; others follow them without knowing why, and a single gesture from them does more than a long speech from someone else. For Nour: authority on the floor comes from knowing the work and staying consistent, so let your example during a crunch carry more weight than long instructions.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 42 'Born to Command' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Think with the Few and speak with the Many (maxim 43). Key points: Openly fighting popular opinion invites offense and danger, so the wise keep their contrary views for a few trusted listeners. Thought stays free even when speech is careful. For Nour: argue out strategy disagreements privately with people you trust, and explain decisions publicly in plain terms, adapting the delivery but never saying something you believe is false.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 43 'Think with the Few and speak with the Many' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Sympathy with great Minds (maxim 44). Key points: There is a natural kinship between people of quality that builds trust with few words and wins favor without effort. Recognising and using that affinity is a real skill. For Nour: when you find a supplier, mentor or builder who thinks the way you do, invest in that relationship, since easy understanding saves a great deal of work later.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 44 'Sympathy with great Minds' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Use, but do not abuse, Cunning (maxim 45). Key points: Craft should be hidden and never boasted of, because visible cunning breeds distrust and revenge; caution is wise, but let skill show in clean execution. For Nour: stay alert to tricks from others, but keep your own dealings so clean that there is nothing clever to hide, whether with customers, the crew or suppliers.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 45 'Use, but do not abuse, Cunning' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Master your Antipathies (maxim 46). Key points: We often dislike people before we know anything about them, and disliking those better than ourselves is especially discrediting. Good sense overrules such reflexes. For Nour: when a new customer or job applicant rubs you the wrong way on sight, give them the same fair hearing and the same honest estimate or interview as anyone else.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 46 'Master your Antipathies' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Avoid "Affairs of Honour" (maxim 47). Key points: Stay out of disputes that hinge on pride, because it is easier to avoid them than to come out of them well, and one quarrel leads to the next. Declining takes more courage than winning. For Nour: when a competitor or an online critic picks a public fight, answer once with facts if needed and then let it go, rather than turning it into a feud.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 47 'Avoid "Affairs of Honour"' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Be Thorough (maxim 48). Key points: Some people are all front: an impressive entrance with nothing behind it, and talk that dries up after the greeting. The substance inside must match the show outside. For Nour: a polished website and admin dashboard mean little if the work in the bays and the data behind the screens do not hold up under a close look.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 48 'Be Thorough' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Observation and Judgment (maxim 49). Key points: A sharp observer reads people and situations quickly, inferring a great deal from small signs, and so masters events instead of being ruled by them. For Nour: watch how customers react while reading an estimate, which lines they question and where they hesitate, and use that to rewrite estimates so they answer those questions up front.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 49 'Observation and Judgment' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Never lose Self-respect (maxim 50). Key points: Make your own conscience the strictest judge of your conduct, and avoid unworthy acts out of self-regard rather than fear of being caught. Then no outside watcher is needed. For Nour: hold yourself to the same standard on the job nobody will inspect, and on the code path nobody will read, as on the ones that get checked.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 50 'Never lose Self-respect' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Know how to Choose well (maxim 51). Key points: Much of life depends on choosing, which takes taste and judgment that intelligence and study alone do not supply; plenty of clever people still pick badly. For Nour: before a big choice such as a new hire, a supplier or a major NOUR OS direction, set the options side by side and choose deliberately instead of grabbing the first acceptable one.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 51 'Know how to Choose well' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Never be put out (maxim 52). Key points: Composure is the mark of a strong character. Passions that spill out through the mouth put reputation at risk, so stay self-possessed in good fortune and bad alike. For Nour: on a day the bays are full and three things break at once, a calm voice at the counter tells customers and the crew that the situation is under control.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 52 'Never be put out' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Diligent and Intelligent (maxim 53). Key points: Careful thought has to be followed by prompt action: fools rush in unprepared, while the wise more often fail through delay. Hurry slowly, but do not leave for tomorrow what can be done today. For Nour: once you have decided on a fix, ship it that day rather than letting a finished plan sit for a week.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 53 'Diligent and Intelligent' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Know how to show your Teeth (maxim 54). Key points: Give way once and you will be pushed again and again, and winning back ground later costs far more. Courage should be kept ready but sheathed in caution, as the bee pairs honey with a sting. For Nour: be easy to deal with, but when a vendor keeps shorting orders or someone tries to bully the crew, set the boundary early and clearly.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 54 'Know how to show your Teeth' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Wait (maxim 55). Key points: Patience and self-mastery come before mastery of others. Time accomplishes more than force, and opportunity arrives only after you have passed through the waiting. For Nour: some things, like a reputation in the neighborhood or a crew that runs smoothly without you, take seasons to build, so measure them by the year rather than the week.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 55 'Wait' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Have Presence of Mind (maxim 56). Key points: Quick wits in the moment head off disaster. Some people think at length and still go wrong, while others do their best work in an emergency. For Nour: write short checklists so the crew can act fast when a car arrives on a tow or a system goes down, because a prepared response is what makes quick thinking reliable.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 56 'Have Presence of Mind' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Slow and Sure (maxim 57). Key points: Doing a thing well matters more than doing it fast. What is done in a hurry is undone in a hurry, and work meant to last needs preparation to match. For Nour: on safety work like brakes or suspension the right job beats the quick job every time, and the same rule applies to database changes in NOUR OS.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 57 'Slow and Sure' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Adapt Yourself to your Company (maxim 58). Key points: Do not display all your ability at once or use more force than the moment requires. Holding something back keeps people interested and leaves room to show more tomorrow. For Nour: do not unload every possible recommendation on a customer in one visit; fix what matters today, note what to watch, and raise the rest when it becomes relevant.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 58 'Adapt Yourself to your Company' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Finish off well (maxim 59). Key points: A graceful exit matters more than a grand entrance. Many begin brilliantly and end badly, and people remember how you leave far more than how you arrived. For Nour: the moment a customer picks up the car, with a clear walk-through of the invoice and the old parts, matters as much as the greeting when they first walked in.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 59 'Finish off well' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: A Sound Judgment (maxim 60). Key points: Some people start with a natural head start in good sense, and experience ripens it into sound judgment that rejects whims, especially where certainty matters most. Such people belong at the helm. For Nour: put those with steady judgment, not just the fastest hands, in charge of calls that matter, and on big decisions prefer the proven option over the clever one.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 60 'A Sound Judgment' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: To Excel in what is Excellent (maxim 61). Key points: Excellence in an important field sets a person apart, while being great at something small brings comfort but little distinction. Mediocrity never earns applause. For Nour: aim for the shop to be known for something customers care about deeply, such as honest diagnosis, rather than being merely decent at everything.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 61 'To Excel in what is Excellent' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Use good Instruments (maxim 62). Key points: Some leaders pick weak helpers so they themselves look clever, which is a dangerous vanity. The world judges the principal by the whole result and hands him all the credit and all the blame. For Nour: hire and keep strong people and choose solid tools, because customers blame the shop, not the individual tech or the software, when a job goes wrong.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 62 'Use good Instruments' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: To be the First of the Kind is an Excellence (maxim 63). Key points: Being first in a field is a major advantage when talent is equal, since latecomers are seen as imitators. The wise look for new paths where they can lead. For Nour: a tire shop running on its own AI operating system is new ground, and being early there is worth more than being a late copy of a bigger chain's playbook.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 63 'To be the First of the Kind is an Excellence' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Avoid Worry (maxim 64). Key points: Prudence that sidesteps trouble is the source of peace. Do not pass on or take in bad news that cannot help, and do not accept lasting trouble to give someone else a moment of satisfaction. For Nour: have Nick filter alerts so only problems you can act on reach your phone, and decline favors that would cost you far more later than they help the asker now.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 64 'Avoid Worry' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Elevated Taste (maxim 65). Key points: Taste can be trained like the intellect, and a high standard should be sparing with approval. Still, finding fault with everything is folly, not refinement. For Nour: raise the bar for how the shop looks and how the software feels by spending time with work you admire, but do not become the owner who criticizes everything the crew does.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 65 'Elevated Taste' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: See that Things end well (maxim 66). Key points: People judge by outcomes, not by the care taken along the way, and a good result covers a lot. Gracián even allows bending the rules of the craft to reach a good end. For Nour: keep the outcome focus but not the license; a customer remembers whether the car was fixed right, so bend internal routines when needed, never the truth on the invoice.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 66 'See that Things end well' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Prefer Callings "en Evidence" (maxim 67). Key points: Work done in public view wins esteem, while equally valuable hidden work goes unnoticed, so prefer roles whose results people can see and use. For Nour: make the shop's good work visible, for example a short note on the invoice listing what was inspected and found fine, because quality nobody sees earns little trust.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 67 'Prefer Callings "en Evidence"' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: It is better to help with Intelligence than with Memory (maxim 68). Key points: Offering what is needed at the right moment beats merely recalling facts; share insight when you have it, ask for it when you lack it, and start with a hint before saying more. Many things fail only because nobody tried. For Nour: Nick should prompt the timely suggestion, not just store notes, and when one approach to a supplier gets a no, look for the version that gets a yes.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 68 'It is better to help with Intelligence than with Memory' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Do not give way to every common Impulse (maxim 69). Key points: A strong person is not swept along by other people's moods or his own. Know your temperament and correct for it, or desire and judgment will pull in opposite directions. For Nour: if you notice you say yes too fast when excited about an idea, make a rule to sleep on it before committing money or the crew's time.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 69 'Do not give way to every common Impulse' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Know how to Refuse (maxim 70). Key points: Refusing well matters as much as agreeing, and a gracious no can satisfy more than a grudging yes. Gracián advises softening refusals and leaving some hope. For Nour: when the shop cannot take a job, say so clearly and kindly and point the customer somewhere useful, but never leave them hoping for something you cannot deliver.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 70 'Know how to Refuse' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Do not Vacillate (maxim 71). Key points: Consistency earns trust. Change your course for good reasons, but people who flip their positions from day to day destroy their own credibility and their standing with others. For Nour: keep shop policies like first come, first served steady, so customers and the crew know exactly what to expect each day.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 71 'Do not Vacillate' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Be Resolute (maxim 72). Key points: Poor execution does less harm than indecision. Some people see clearly yet cannot act and always need someone else to decide, while the able find a way through and move on to the next thing. For Nour: when a decision is stuck between two reasonable options, pick one and set a date to review it, rather than letting the shop or a build lane wait on you.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 72 'Be Resolute' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Utilise Slips (maxim 73). Key points: Clever people escape tight spots with a light remark or a change of subject, and sometimes the wisest move is to seem not to understand. For Nour: a little humor can ease a tense moment at the counter, but never use deflection to dodge a customer's real question about their bill or their car.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 73 'Utilise Slips' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Do not be Unsociable (maxim 74). Key points: People who turn haughty and hard to reach once they gain a position lose the goodwill that got them there. Being accessible is part of the job, not a favor. For Nour: as the shop grows, stay reachable to the crew and to any customer with a problem, even when NOUR OS handles most routine questions.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 74 'Do not be Unsociable' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Choose an Heroic Ideal (maxim 75). Key points: Pick the best in your field as a spur, aiming to rival them rather than copy them. Another person's fame can feed generous ambition instead of envy. For Nour: study the best-run independent shops and the best software builders, then use their standard to push your own work, not to clone their look.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 75 'Choose an Heroic Ideal' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Do not always be Jesting (maxim 76). Key points: Constant joking costs credibility: like a known liar, the habitual joker is never quite believed, and people cannot tell when he means it. Wit has its moment, and seriousness should have the rest. For Nour: keep the shop friendly, but when explaining a safety issue or a price, make sure the customer can tell you mean every word.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 76 'Do not always be Jesting' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Be all Things to all Men (maxim 77). Key points: Adapt to each person's mood and level, serious or light as the moment calls for, which wins broad goodwill but takes real skill. For Nour: adapt the tone, never the facts; talk shop with a car enthusiast and keep it simple for someone who just wants the car safe, but give both the same honest assessment.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 77 'Be all Things to all Men' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: The Art of undertaking Things (maxim 78). Key points: Fools rush in with no precautions and feel no shame when they fail. Prudence advances carefully, testing the depth before each step, because there are hidden depths in dealings with people. For Nour: before a big change such as a new pricing approach or a data migration, try it small and check the results before rolling it out everywhere.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 78 'The Art of undertaking Things' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: A Genial Disposition (maxim 79). Key points: A touch of cheerfulness, kept within the bounds of dignity, makes people like you, and taking some things lightly shows a forgiving nature that draws others in. For Nour: a good-humored owner sets the tone for a long Saturday on the floor, so laugh off small mishaps and keep the crew loose without letting standards slip.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 79 'A Genial Disposition' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Take care to get Information (maxim 80). Key points: We rely on reports far more than on our own eyes, and every report is colored by whoever passed it along. Weigh praise with care and blame with even more care, and consider the speaker's motive. For Nour: when you hear about a problem secondhand, check the source and the record, such as the invoice or the call log, before acting on it.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 80 'Take care to get Information' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Renew your Brilliance (maxim 81). Key points: Ability and fame grow stale with familiarity, and a fresh mediocrity can outshine an excellence everyone is used to. Keep renewing yourself, and now and then change the stage you work on. For Nour: refresh how the shop shows up, its photos, its messages and its services, before customers stop noticing, and keep learning new skills yourself.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 81 'Renew your Brilliance' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Drain Nothing to the Dregs, neither Good nor Ill (maxim 82). Key points: Virtue sits in the middle; push even a good thing to its extreme and it turns bad, and overworking an idea makes it dull. For Nour: do not squeeze every last hour out of the crew or every last dollar out of a single job, because pressing too hard turns a good arrangement sour.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 82 'Drain Nothing to the Dregs, neither Good nor Ill' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Allow Yourself some venial Fault (maxim 83). Key points: Envy attacks anything that looks flawless, so Gracián suggests showing a small harmless imperfection, though never in prudence, to take the edge off malice. For Nour: you do not need to look perfect, and you should not fake flaws either; openly owning a real small mistake to a customer builds more trust than a polished image ever will.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 83 'Allow Yourself some venial Fault' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Make use of your Enemies (maxim 84). Key points: Take hold of things by the safe end, not the sharp one. A wise person gains more from enemies than a fool does from friends, since hostility can be an honest mirror while flattery hides the flaws. For Nour: read a harsh review or a competitor's jab for the part that is true, fix that part, and let the rest go.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 84 'Make use of your Enemies' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Do not play Manille (maxim 85). Key points: Like the trump card played every hand, excellence that is overused gets cheap, and being useful to everyone wears out your welcome. Be exceptional in substance but modest in display. For Nour: do not push the shop's message everywhere at once until people tune it out; show up where it counts and let the work speak.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 85 'Do not play Manille' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Prevent Scandal (maxim 86). Key points: A single bad story, especially one with a catchy label attached, can stick and damage a reputation, and clearing your name is much harder than keeping it clean. Prevention beats repair. For Nour: handle a customer complaint quickly and fairly before it becomes the story people tell about the shop.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 86 'Prevent Scandal' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Culture and Elegance (maxim 87). Key points: Learning lifts a person above raw instinct, but knowledge without refinement is still coarse; thought, desire and especially speech should all be polished. For Nour: keep learning beyond cars and code, in subjects like history, writing and design, and let it sharpen how you speak to customers, the crew and anyone you build with.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 87 'Culture and Elegance' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Let your Behaviour be Fine and Noble (maxim 88). Key points: A leader should not be petty. He need not dig into every unpleasant detail, since knowing everything is not the same as knowing all about everything, and overlooking much is part of ruling well. For Nour: let a small slip by the crew pass once it is corrected rather than auditing every minor error, and save your attention for patterns that matter.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 88 'Let your Behaviour be Fine and Noble' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Know Yourself (maxim 89). Key points: A face can be checked in a glass, but the mind has no such mirror, so careful self-reflection has to serve instead. Know your abilities, judgment and courage in order to govern yourself. For Nour: once a month, review your own decisions against how they turned out, and let Nick keep that record so the lessons stick.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 89 'Know Yourself' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: The Secret of Long Life (maxim 90). Key points: Live well: folly and vice shorten a life, while steadiness of character carries over into the body. A good life lasts longer in practice as well as in purpose. For Nour: a sustainable pace and clean habits are what let you run the shop and build NOUR OS for decades, not just through the next busy season.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 90 'The Secret of Long Life' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Never set to work at anything if you have any doubts of its Prudence (maxim 91). Key points: If the person acting doubts a plan, onlookers will be sure it fails, and a scruple felt in the moment usually becomes regret later. Do not act on a plan your own reason already rejects. For Nour: when your gut says a deal or a shortcut is wrong, stop and find out why before going ahead.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 91 'Never set to work at anything if you have any doubts of its Prudence' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Transcendant Wisdom (maxim 92). Key points: Sound judgment beats cleverness in every matter, and it counts for more the greater your responsibility. Satisfy the wise and you have truly succeeded, even without applause. For Nour: a plain, sensible decision that Mash and Manny can carry out beats a clever system nobody on the floor understands.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 92 'Transcendant Wisdom' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Versatility (maxim 93). Key points: A person with many skills is worth several people and enriches the lives of those around him. Cultivate a broad range of tastes and abilities. For Nour: cross-training pays off; a crew where people can cover the counter, tires and lighter repairs keeps the shop moving when someone is out, much as Zach already works across roles.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 93 'Versatility' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Keep the extent of your Abilities unknown (maxim 94). Key points: Gracián advises letting people see your abilities without letting them measure their limits, because uncertainty about your depth earns more respect than exact knowledge of it. For Nour: the honest version is to keep growing so there is always more depth than people expect, while never overstating what you or the shop can actually do.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 94 'Keep the extent of your Abilities unknown' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Keep Expectation alive (maxim 95). Key points: Keep people looking forward: let each achievement hint at a larger one, and never stake everything on a single throw. Pacing your efforts keeps interest from fading. For Nour: release NOUR OS improvements steadily instead of in one big drop, so each step builds confidence and no single launch carries all the risk.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 95 'Keep Expectation alive' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: The highest Discretion (maxim 96). Key points: Good judgment is the foundation of prudence and lets you succeed at little cost; it is the one quality whose absence spoils all the others. It is a natural lean toward the sensible course and the safe one. For Nour: when in doubt about customer data or a risky change, choose the path that can be undone.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 96 'The highest Discretion' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Obtain and preserve a Reputation (maxim 97). Key points: A reputation is costly to earn because it rests on rare ability, but once won it is fairly easy to keep and brings many benefits. Only one built on real merit lasts. For Nour: the shop's name is built one honest invoice at a time, and it should be guarded with the same care every day.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 97 'Obtain and preserve a Reputation' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Write your Intentions in Cypher (maxim 98). Key points: Gracián advises hiding your passions and even your preferences, so others cannot exploit them by flattering or opposing you. Showing your whole hand risks the stakes. For Nour: in a negotiation with a supplier, do not reveal how badly you want the deal, but be fully open with customers and the crew about what you expect from them.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 98 'Write your Intentions in Cypher' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Reality and Appearance (maxim 99). Key points: People judge by how things look, not by how they are, and few look beneath the surface. Being right is not enough if it looks wrong. For Nour: an honest repair recommendation can look like an upsell, so show the evidence and explain the reason, so the truth also looks true to the customer.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 99 'Reality and Appearance' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: A Man without Illusions, a wise Christian, a philosophic Courtier (maxim 100). Key points: Gracián asks you to truly be clear-sighted, good and thoughtful, not merely to seem so or pretend. Careful thinking and seeing through deceit are what feed a sound mind. For Nour: be the real thing rather than the image, an owner who thinks clearly and acts decently when no one is watching, and keep testing your own assumptions.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 100 'A Man without Illusions, a wise Christian, a philosophic Courtier' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: One half of the World laughs at the other, and Fools are they all (maxim 101). Key points: Every taste has its fans and its critics, so no single verdict makes a thing good or bad. Do not bend everything to your own preferences, and do not let one person's praise or scorn steer you; weigh the opinion of people who actually know the craft. For Nour: one angry walk-in or one glowing comment is a data point, not a verdict; judge a change by the trend across many counter invoices.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 101 'One half of the World laughs at the other, and Fools are they all' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Be able to stomach big slices of Luck (maxim 102). Key points: A capable person can absorb sudden success without losing balance, while a small spirit is thrown off by a windfall and turns vain or reckless. Show that you have room to grow into bigger things. For Nour: when a record week hits the counter, treat it as a stress test of the systems, not a reason to loosen standards; check that intake, parts and the crew actually held up under the load.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 102 'Be able to stomach big slices of Luck' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Let each keep up his Dignity (maxim 103). Key points: Whatever your rank, hold yourself to the standards of someone at the top: upright in conduct and high in thought. Real stature comes from integrity, not titles or ceremony, so copy the substance of greatness and skip its show. For Nour: run a neighborhood tire shop with the integrity a big operator only claims; an honest estimate written cleanly on a slow day is the dignity, not the sign out front.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 103 'Let each keep up his Dignity' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Try your hand at Office (maxim 104). Key points: Every role asks for different strengths: some need courage, some tact, and the hardest need cleverness on top of character. Leading people is demanding work, and the best posts give room for judgment and variety rather than a rigid rut. For Nour: when you hand Mash or Manny a new responsibility, name which strength it calls for, steadiness or judgment, so they know what good looks like in that seat.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 104 'Try your hand at Office' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Don't be a Bore (maxim 105). Key points: People with one topic wear others out. Short, well-chosen words do more business and earn more goodwill than a pile of detail, and the busiest people deserve brevity most. For Nour: when Nick reports to you, it should lead with the answer and stop; the same rule applies when the counter explains a repair to a customer who is short on time.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 105 'Don't be a Bore' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Do not parade your Position (maxim 106). Key points: Flaunting rank breeds envy, and respect cannot be demanded, only earned from others. Keep enough authority to do the job, but let people value you for ability rather than title; anyone who insists on deference shows they have not earned it. For Nour: the crew should follow you because you can diagnose the hard car and make the fair call, never because you remind them who owns the shop.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 106 'Do not parade your Position' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Show no Self-satisfaction (maxim 107). Key points: Steer between running yourself down and admiring yourself; smugness usually comes from not knowing what you lack. A little self-doubt is useful, since it prepares you for setbacks and softens them when they arrive. For Nour: after a feature ships to NOUR OS, assume something in it is still wrong and go looking for it; the bug you expected never ambushes you.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 107 'Show no Self-satisfaction' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: The Path to Greatness is along with Others (maxim 108). Key points: Good sense and skill rub off through company, and pairing opposite temperaments finds a balanced middle without forcing it. Getting along well with others is a real art. For Nour: pair a fast, confident tech with a careful one on a tricky diagnosis; the mix of speed and caution catches what either would miss working alone.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 108 'The Path to Greatness is along with Others' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Be not Censorious (maxim 109). Key points: Some people find fault with everything by nature, blowing small flaws into crimes and turning any workplace into a prison. A generous mind looks for an excuse for a mistake, if not in the intent, then in simple oversight. For Nour: when a ticket is entered wrong at the counter, assume a rushed moment before assuming carelessness, fix the process, and keep the person's dignity intact.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 109 'Be not Censorious' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Do not wait till you are a Sinking Sun (maxim 110). Key points: Leave a thing before it leaves you. Step away while you can still go out on a win, rather than waiting until the decline is obvious and people have turned cold. For Nour: retire a NOUR OS feature or a shop routine while it still works but is fading, before it becomes the thing everyone quietly works around.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 110 'Do not wait till you are a Sinking Sun' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Have Friends (maxim 111). Key points: Friends are a second life. People tend to become what others wish for them, so win hearts with good turns, since kind acts are the surest route to friendly feeling. Try each day to make one well-wisher; some will become close over time. For Nour: an honest favor to a neighboring business on Euclid Ave, done without keeping score, builds a network no advertising can buy.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 111 'Have Friends' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Gain Good-will (maxim 112). Key points: Merit alone travels slowly; goodwill speeds everything up, fills in gaps, and overlooks small faults because it is not hunting for them. It grows from shared interests, and it is hard to win but easy to keep once held. For Nour: a customer who trusts the shop forgives a busy Saturday; earn that trust with straight talk on the first visit, because winning it is the hard part.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 112 'Gain Good-will' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: In Prosperity prepare for Adversity (maxim 113). Key points: Gather supplies for winter in summer. When things go well, favors are cheap and friends plentiful, so bank goodwill then for the lean days when help is scarce and costly. Small minds ignore friends in good times and get ignored in bad ones. For Nour: in a strong month, build the cash cushion and pay suppliers promptly; that record is what earns you flexibility when a slow month arrives.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 113 'In Prosperity prepare for Adversity' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Never Compete (maxim 114). Key points: Open rivalry harms your name: competitors dig up old faults that courtesy would have left buried, and the fight splashes mud on both sides. Good repute lasts longest where you are not locked in a feud. For Nour: never run down other shops online or at the counter; win on how cars and customers are treated, and let the comparison happen in the customer's own head.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 114 'Never Compete' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Get used to the Failings of your Familiars (maxim 115). Key points: People you depend on, or who depend on you, will have irritating flaws. Get used to them early, the way you stop noticing a plain face, so you are not forced to adjust in a crisis. For Nour: every crew member has a habit that grates; decide calmly which ones matter to the work and which you will simply live with, before a packed Saturday decides for you.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 115 'Get used to the Failings of your Familiars' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Only act with Honourable Men (maxim 116). Key points: People of honor can be trusted even in a disagreement, because they act true to who they are; a quarrel with them beats a win over the dishonest. Those without honor give no real guarantee, whatever the contract says. For Nour: choose suppliers and partners by how they behaved when something went wrong, not by the terms they offered; a clean argument with an honest vendor is worth more.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 116 'Only act with Honourable Men' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Never talk of Yourself (maxim 117). Key points: Talking about yourself forces either boasting, which is vain, or self-criticism, which looks small, and both sit badly with listeners. The same trap waits when you discuss someone to their face, where you drift toward flattery or attack. For Nour: on the shop's social posts, show the work and the customer's car, not the owner; let the result do the talking.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 117 'Never talk of Yourself' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Acquire the Reputation of Courtesy (maxim 118). Key points: Courtesy alone is enough to make people like you; it costs little and returns much. Err toward too much rather than too little, fit it to the person, and show it especially to opponents. The honor you give stays with you. For Nour: every walk-in gets a respectful greeting, and the customer who arrived angry gets the most patience, since courtesy toward an opponent is a sign of strength.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 118 'Acquire the Reputation of Courtesy' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Avoid becoming Disliked (maxim 119). Key points: Dislike arrives without invitation, and once rooted it is as hard to remove as a bad name. Arrogance draws disdain and clowning draws contempt, so give respect in order to receive it. For Nour: a single dismissive remark to a customer can outlast a hundred good jobs; make sure everyone at the counter treats even a difficult caller with plain respect.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 119 'Avoid becoming Disliked' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Live Practically (maxim 120). Key points: Ideas and tastes shift with the times, so keep your methods current and meet people where they are, hoping to lead them somewhere better later. The exception is goodness: honesty and keeping your word never expire, even when they look unfashionable. Make the most of what you have. For Nour: adopt new tools in NOUR OS when they help, but never let a marketing trend loosen the shop's honesty with customers.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 120 'Live Practically' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Do not make a Business of what is no Business (maxim 121). Key points: Some people turn every trifle into a dispute or a secret. Minor troubles often fade if left alone, while fussing can make them real, and a cure can create the illness. Settle what matters early and let the rest go. For Nour: not every odd log line in NOUR OS deserves a new PR; fix the ones that touch customers or money and let the noise stay noise.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 121 'Do not make a Business of what is no Business' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Distinction in Speech and Action (maxim 122). Key points: A quiet, earned air of authority in how you speak and carry yourself wins respect before you even arrive. It does not come from pompous talk but from real ability backed by merit. For Nour: a diagnosis explained calmly at the counter, with the old part in hand, earns more trust than any slogan on the wall.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 122 'Distinction in Speech and Action' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Avoid Affectation (maxim 123). Key points: The greater your merit, the less you should put on airs; affectation makes real virtues look fake and wears out everyone, including you. Hide the effort behind good work, but do not fake naturalness either. For Nour: keep the shop's voice plain and direct; customer copy that strains to sound impressive reads as a sales pitch, and customers can tell.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 123 'Avoid Affectation' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Get Yourself missed (maxim 124). Key points: Most people are forgotten once their work is done. The way to be missed is to excel in your role and be pleasant with it, so the post needs you more than you need the post. Being missed only because a successor is worse is no real honor. For Nour: make the shop so good that customers notice the difference when they try elsewhere, through better work, never by making it hard to leave.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 124 'Get Yourself missed' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Do not be a Black List (maxim 125). Key points: Keeping a tally of other people's scandals stains you more than them; it is often a way to hide your own faults or console yourself. Digging in dirt only dirties the digger. For Nour: when shop talk turns to another shop's mistakes or a former employee's failings, steer it back to the work in the bay.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 125 'Do not be a Black List' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Folly consists not in committing Folly, but in not hiding it when committed (maxim 126). Key points: Everyone makes mistakes; Gracian's point is that the wise keep their errors out of view while fools parade them, since reputation rides on what stays hidden. He pairs it with a second rule: learn to forget. For Nour: never hide a mistake from a customer it affects; own it and fix it. Use the maxim only to stop dwelling on or broadcasting old blunders once they are corrected.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 126 'Folly consists not in committing Folly, but in not hiding it when committed' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Grace in Everything (maxim 127). Key points: Grace is the finishing touch that brings talent, speech and action to life. It is mostly natural, it beats training, and it gets you out of awkward moments quickly; without it even beauty feels lifeless. For Nour: a hard conversation about a declined estimate goes better with an easy, unhurried manner than with a perfect script; teach the counter the tone, not only the words.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 127 'Grace in Everything' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Highmindedness (maxim 128). Key points: A lofty spirit is a core trait of a person of quality: it refines taste, lifts the heart, and can even repair bad turns of fortune. Generosity and courage grow from it, and it can live in intention even when action is blocked. For Nour: on a bad week, hold the standard you would hold on a good one; generous treatment of a stranded driver is high-mindedness in practice.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 128 'Highmindedness' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Never complain (maxim 129). Key points: Complaining lowers your standing: it invites pity instead of respect, shows others where to hurt you, and turns one insult into an excuse for the next. Praising favors you have received does more, nudging others to match them. For Nour: in vendor calls and in front of the crew, talk about who helped the shop this month rather than who let it down, and take grievances straight to the person who can fix them.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 129 'Never complain' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Do and be seen Doing (maxim 130). Key points: People judge by appearances, so being useful and showing that you are useful doubles your value. Unseen work counts as if it never happened, and even a right action loses credit if it does not look right. For Nour: photograph the worn part, show it to the customer, and note it on the invoice; good work the customer cannot see earns no trust.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 130 'Do and be seen Doing' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Nobility of Feeling (maxim 131). Key points: A rare greatness of soul speaks well of enemies and treats them even better, and it shines most when revenge is within reach, turning a full victory into a show of generosity. It claims no credit and keeps its merit quiet. For Nour: if someone who wronged the shop later comes in needing help, treat them fairly and well; that is the strongest answer there is.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 131 'Nobility of Feeling' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Revise your Judgments (maxim 132). Key points: Running a decision past an inner court of review makes it safer and buys time to confirm or improve it. A considered gift is valued more, a delayed refusal stings less, and someone pressing hard for an instant answer is often trying to catch you off guard. For Nour: when a sales rep pushes for a same-day yes on a new system, sleep on it and have Nick check the claims first.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 132 'Revise your Judgments' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Better Mad with the rest of the World than Wise alone (maxim 133). Key points: Gracian reports the politician's view that solitary wisdom looks like folly and it pays to move with the current, then turns it around: better to be sensible alongside others than a fool on your own. Chasing originality for its own sake is chasing fantasies. For Nour: use standard, proven tools for NOUR OS where they work, and spend originality only where the shop is genuinely different.
