entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 133 'Better Mad with the rest of the World than Wise alone' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Double your Resources (maxim 134). Key points: Never depend on one thing, however strong, because whatever rests on human favor is fragile. Keep the sources of success doubled, the way nature gives us two of our most exposed limbs. For Nour: no single supplier, lead channel or tech should be a point of failure; keep a second vendor for common parts and cross-train so the bay keeps moving when someone is out.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 134 'Double your Resources' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Do not nourish the Spirit of Contradiction (maxim 135). Key points: Habitually finding fault with everything may look clever but marks you as foolish or sour. Such people turn friendly talk into combat and treat their own associates like enemies. For Nour: in a planning session with Nick or the crew, push back when it matters, but do not argue every point for sport; constant objection teaches people to stop bringing you ideas.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 135 'Do not nourish the Spirit of Contradiction' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Post Yourself in the Centre of Things (maxim 136). Key points: Stand where you can feel the pulse of the matter. Many lose themselves in side branches and wordy debate, circling a point a hundred times without reaching the core, then lack time for what counts. For Nour: when a weekly review sprawls, ask the central question first: how many counter invoices closed this week compared with last, and what explains the difference?
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 136 'Post Yourself in the Centre of Things' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: The Sage should be Self-sufficing (maxim 137). Key points: A person who is complete within carries everything with them and can stand alone, needing no one else's judgment or taste to function. Gracian ranks that self-sufficiency among the highest forms of contentment. For Nour: keep the habit of deciding from your own clear reasoning and evidence, so that no single adviser or tool, Nick included, becomes something you cannot think without.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 137 'The Sage should be Self-sufficing' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: The Art of letting Things alone (maxim 138). Key points: In the storms of public or private life it is often wise to ride at anchor and wait. A good doctor knows when not to treat, and stirred water clears by being left alone, not by more meddling. For Nour: when a customer dispute flares or the crew is heated, do not force a resolution on the spot; let it cool for a day, then settle it calmly.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 138 'The Art of letting Things alone' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Recognise unlucky Days (maxim 139). Key points: Some days nothing goes right, and a couple of attempts will tell you which kind of day it is. On good days seize every opening; on bad ones, do not force big moves, and do not judge the day from one small win or one small annoyance. For Nour: if a deploy fails twice while the bay is backed up, hold the risky merge until tomorrow and spend the day on safe work.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 139 'Recognise unlucky Days' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Find the Good in a Thing at once (maxim 140). Key points: Good taste goes looking for what is valuable, the way a bee finds honey where a snake finds venom. Some fixate on one flaw among a thousand merits; the luckier spot one merit among many faults. For Nour: when reviewing a new hire's first week, start with what they did well and build on it before listing what to correct.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 140 'Find the Good in a Thing at once' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Do not listen to Yourself (maxim 141). Key points: Pleasing yourself means little if you do not please others, and the attention you spend admiring your own words is owed to your listeners. People who pause after every sentence for approval wear everyone out. For Nour: when explaining a repair, watch the customer's face rather than polishing your own explanation; their confusion is the signal, not your phrasing.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 141 'Do not listen to Yourself' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Never from Obstinacy take the Wrong Side because your Opponent has anticipated you in taking the Right One (maxim 142). Key points: If a rival takes the correct position first, do not grab the wrong one just to oppose them; you start that fight already beaten. Stubbornness throws away truth by contradicting it. The wise side with what is right, whoever got there first. For Nour: if another shop beats you to a good idea, adopt the good idea openly instead of defending a worse one out of pride.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 142 'Never from Obstinacy take the Wrong Side because your Opponent has anticipated you in taking the Right One' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Never become Paradoxical in order to avoid the Trite (maxim 143). Key points: Fleeing the ordinary into the eccentric hurts your standing as much as being dull. Paradox wins early applause through novelty, then collapses once people see it is empty; it is the detour of those who cannot reach excellence directly. For Nour: shop marketing does not need clever contrarian hooks; plain, true statements about the work outlast stunts.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 143 'Never become Paradoxical in order to avoid the Trite' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Begin with Another's to end with your Own (maxim 144). Key points: Gracian describes a tactic of opening with the other person's interest as a lure, so your own aim advances under cover; it works best on people who refuse by reflex. It is persuasion by framing. For Nour: use only the honest version; lead with what the customer actually needs, never dress up an upsell as their idea, and when the shop's interest and theirs line up, say both plainly.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 144 'Begin with Another's to end with your Own' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Do not show your wounded Finger (maxim 145). Key points: Expose a sore spot and everything will bump into it, because ill-will aims exactly where you are weak. The wise do not admit being hit, and they keep the sources of both pain and joy private, so the one fades and the other lasts. For Nour: do not vent shop frustrations on public pages or in front of customers; handle the sore point privately with the person who can fix it.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 145 'Do not show your wounded Finger' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Look into the Interior of Things (maxim 146). Key points: Things are usually different from how they look. Falsehood arrives first and sweeps the careless along; truth comes last, slowly, carried by time. The prudent hold back part of their judgment to wait for it. For Nour: when a car arrives with a confident diagnosis from another shop or a code reader, verify it in the bay before quoting; the first story is often wrong.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 146 'Look into the Interior of Things' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Do not be Inaccessible (maxim 147). Key points: No one is so capable that they never need advice; the person nobody dares correct falls with no one to pull them out. Keep a door open to a trusted friend who is free to advise and even rebuke you. For Nour: give Mash and Manny explicit permission to tell you when one of your calls is wrong, and thank them when they do.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 147 'Do not be Inaccessible' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Have the Art of Conversation (maxim 148). Key points: Conversation reveals who you are; it is the most ordinary act and needs the most care. Be plain with friends, more formal where respect is due, and match the other person's mind and tone. Do not nitpick words or ration ideas, and value discretion over eloquence. For Nour: speak differently to a nervous first-time customer and to a fleet manager; adjust the depth, keep the facts identical.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 148 'Have the Art of Conversation' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Know how to put off Ills on Others (maxim 149). Key points: Gracian advises a leader to keep someone in place to absorb blame and resentment, since not every venture can succeed or satisfy everyone. It is a shield against ill-will, paid for with some pride. For Nour: take the opposite lesson; never let a crew member carry the blame for your decision. If you need a shield, make it a written policy that everyone, including you, follows.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 149 'Know how to put off Ills on Others' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Know to get your Price for Things (maxim 150). Key points: Real worth is not enough, because most people follow the crowd and never look beneath the surface. Gracian suggests building repute through praise, a striking name and an air of the uncommon, without affectation, and warns against calling your goods cheap or ordinary. For Nour: explain the shop's services clearly so their value shows, but never invent scarcity or inflate a claim; describe real quality honestly.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 150 'Know to get your Price for Things' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Think beforehand (maxim 151). Key points: Plan today for tomorrow and for many days beyond, and above all foresee when trouble will come. Thinking before you are stuck beats scrambling later; many act first and then hunt for excuses rather than weighing consequences. For Nour: before the first cold snap, list what slowed the bay last winter and line up parts and crew coverage now, instead of solving it with customers already at the counter.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 151 'Think beforehand' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Never have a Companion who casts you in the Shade (maxim 152). Key points: Gracian warns against partners who outshine you, since you will always play second to them; choose those who set you off instead, though never at the cost of bad company. Keep eminent company while rising and ordinary company once arrived. For Nour: reject the vanity in this one; hire and partner with people better than you at their craft, because the shop shines when its best tech outshines its owner.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 152 'Never have a Companion who casts you in the Shade' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Beware of entering where there is a great Gap to be filled (maxim 153). Key points: Following a well-loved predecessor is hard because the past always looks better, and merely matching them is not enough; you must clearly exceed them. It is also good policy to leave a role so your successor makes people miss you. For Nour: when you replace a familiar shop routine or tool, the new one must be visibly better on day one, or the crew will keep wishing for the old way.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 153 'Beware of entering where there is a great Gap to be filled' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Do not Believe, or Like, lightly (maxim 154). Key points: A mature mind believes slowly, because lies are common and the easily led soon lose respect. Still, do not insult an informant by openly doubting them; suspend judgment quietly. The same caution applies to liking people quickly, since deeds can deceive as well as words. For Nour: when a new vendor makes big promises, listen politely, then test them with a small order before committing.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 154 'Do not Believe, or Like, lightly' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: The Art of getting into a Passion (maxim 155). Key points: Meet provocation with reflection when you can. If anger is warranted, announce it, so you begin in control, and use only as much as the situation needs. Knowing where to stop is the hardest part, so stay clear-eyed even at the peak. For Nour: if a supplier keeps shorting orders, say plainly that you are angry and why, set the line, and end the call before it turns into venting.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 155 'The Art of getting into a Passion' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Select your Friends (maxim 156). Key points: Choose friends deliberately, after experience and fortune have tested them, since you are judged by the company you keep. Enjoying someone's company is not proof of friendship, and most friends attach to your circumstances rather than to you. A wise friend keeps worries away; a foolish one creates them. For Nour: pick the people you lean on for advice about the shop for judgment proven over time, not for being fun to talk to.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 156 'Select your Friends' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Do not make Mistakes about Character (maxim 157). Key points: Misjudging character is the worst error and the easiest one to make; it is better to overpay than to be sold poor quality, and people need to be studied as carefully as books. For Nour: when hiring a tech, give more weight to how they handled a past mistake than to how smoothly they interview; character shows up in the bay long after the resume is forgotten.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 157 'Do not make Mistakes about Character' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Make use of your Friends (maxim 158). Key points: Using friendships well takes discretion: some friends are best at a distance, some up close. Keeping friends matters more than making them, so choose ones that wear well over time. Friendship multiplies the good and divides the trouble. For Nour: lean on each trusted contact for what they are actually good at, a parts rep for sourcing, a fellow owner for staffing advice, and keep those ties warm between favors.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 158 'Make use of your Friends' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Put up with Fools (maxim 159). Key points: The more you know, the less patience you have for foolishness, yet patience is half of wisdom and the source of peace. We often have to bear the most from those we depend on most. For Nour: a customer who argues the obvious or a vendor who repeats the same error tests your patience; stay steady, because the calm you keep becomes the shop's reputation.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 159 'Put up with Fools' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Be careful in Speaking (maxim 160). Key points: Guard your words with rivals out of prudence and with everyone else for the sake of appearances. You can always add a word later but can never take one back, so speak as carefully as if you were signing a contract. For Nour: whatever the counter says about how a repair will turn out becomes a promise in the customer's mind; say what you know, not what you hope.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 160 'Be careful in Speaking' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Know your pet Faults (maxim 161). Key points: Even the best people have favorite flaws, often tied to their strengths, and the real danger is loving them rather than being unaware of them. Others will dwell on that one blot to dim everything else. For Nour: name your own pet fault plainly, for example starting a new build before the last one ships, and let Nick hold you to the rule that counters it.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 161 'Know your pet Faults' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: How to triumph over Rivals and Detractors (maxim 162). Key points: Contempt for detractors is not enough; a gallant bearing works better. Speaking well of those who speak ill of you, and answering envy with real achievement, is the strongest revenge, since every success torments the envious. For Nour: when someone bad-mouths the shop, do not answer in kind; answer with better work and one calm, courteous reply.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 162 'How to triumph over Rivals and Detractors' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Never, from Sympathy with the Unfortunate, involve Yourself in his Fate (maxim 163). Key points: Gracian notes that the unlucky attract sympathy that does them little good, and that people who bind themselves to a falling person often fall with them; he calls it noble but not worldly-wise. For Nour: help people in trouble, a stranded driver or a struggling acquaintance, with what you can afford to give, but never tie the shop's survival to rescuing someone else's failing venture.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 163 'Never, from Sympathy with the Unfortunate, involve Yourself in his Fate' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Throw Straws in the Air (maxim 164). Key points: Test how something will be received before committing, especially when the outcome is uncertain. A trial run tells you whether to proceed in earnest or quietly withdraw, and it shows where other people stand. For Nour: pilot a new NOUR OS feature with a small slice of real use first, read the reaction, then roll it out or drop it.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 164 'Throw Straws in the Air' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Wage War Honourably (maxim 165). Key points: You may be forced into conflict but never into poisoned weapons; win in a way that does you credit. Never turn confidences from an ended friendship into ammunition, since the smallest treachery stains a name. Be someone in whom loyalty and generosity could still be found. For Nour: in a dispute with a former vendor or employee, never use what they told you in trust; argue the facts only.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 165 'Wage War Honourably' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Distinguish the Man of Words from the Man of Deeds (maxim 166). Key points: Good words paired with bad deeds are worse than bad words. You cannot live on talk or politeness; words should be pledges of work, and a tree with leaves but no fruit offers only shade. For Nour: judge a vendor, a hire or an AI tool by delivered results in the logs and on the invoices, not by its demo or its sales pitch.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 166 'Distinguish the Man of Words from the Man of Deeds' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Know how to take your own Part (maxim 167). Key points: In a crisis a bold heart is your best companion, and if it weakens, shore it up from your other strengths. Do not surrender to misfortune; many double their troubles by not knowing how to carry them. For Nour: when a bad week stacks up, write down what is in your control today and act on the first item, rather than waiting for things to ease on their own.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 167 'Know how to take your own Part' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Do not indulge in the Eccentricities of Folly (maxim 168). Key points: Vanity, caprice, obstinacy, theatrics, nosiness and every kind of one-sidedness are deformities of the mind, worse than any of the body. Without self-control no advice can help, and such people mistake imagined applause for the real ridicule around them. For Nour: watch for whims creeping into shop decisions, such as changing a working process because it bores you; consistency is what the crew relies on.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 168 'Do not indulge in the Eccentricities of Folly' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Be more careful not to Miss once than to Hit a hundred times (maxim 169). Key points: People ignore the sun at full blaze and stare at an eclipse; talk counts the failures, not the wins. A single small blemish can outweigh a long record of good work, because people who wish you harm count each slip and skip each win. For Nour: one car leaving with a loose lug nut can undo many clean jobs, so the final torque check belongs on every wheel, every time.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 169 'Be more careful not to Miss once than to Hit a hundred times' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: In all Things keep Something in Reserve (maxim 170). Key points: Do not spend all your strength or knowledge at once; keep a rearguard so there is something to fall back on when defeat looms. In this matter half can be worth more than the whole. For Nour: keep a cash buffer, extra stock of the fastest-moving parts and some headroom in the crew's day, so a surprise rush or a breakdown does not break the shop.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 170 'In all Things keep Something in Reserve' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Waste not Influence (maxim 171). Key points: Powerful friends are for big occasions; spending a great favor on a small matter wastes it. Keep your sheet anchor for the real emergency, since a favor is among the most costly and valuable things there are. For Nour: do not burn a key supplier contact's goodwill on a rush you could have planned for; save that call for the day a customer is truly stranded.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 171 'Waste not Influence' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Never contend with a Man who has nothing to Lose (maxim 172). Key points: Fighting someone with nothing at stake is an uneven contest: they come in without fear or shame, while you risk a reputation built over years in a single moment. Even a win cannot recover what the exposure costs. For Nour: do not get drawn into a public back-and-forth with an anonymous hostile poster; reply once, calmly and factually, and let it go.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 172 'Never contend with a Man who has nothing to Lose' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Do not be Glass in Intercourse, still less in Friendship (maxim 173). Key points: Some people crack at the lightest touch, imagining slights and hostile intent, so everyone around them tiptoes; they are usually ruled by their moods. A true friend's disposition is firm and lasting. For Nour: build a shop where feedback on the work does not have to be wrapped in cotton, and model it by taking criticism of your own calls without bristling.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 173 'Do not be Glass in Intercourse, still less in Friendship' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Do not live in a Hurry (maxim 174). Key points: Spacing things out is how you enjoy them. Some run through their fortune before their life ends, rushing pleasures they never taste. Go slow in enjoyment and quick in work, since finished work brings satisfaction and finished pleasure brings regret. For Nour: move fast on the repair queue, but do not rush the parts of life outside the shop; a day off is not a backlog to clear.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 174 'Do not live in a Hurry' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: A Solid Man (maxim 175). Key points: A person of substance takes no pleasure in those without it. Some prefer a lie that promises much over a truth that delivers little, but anything built on nothing collapses, and one deceit needs many more to prop it up. Only truth gives lasting reputation. For Nour: every claim on the website and at the counter should be one the shop can back up today; overpromising never lasts.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 175 'A Solid Man' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Have Knowledge, or know those that have Knowledge (maxim 176). Key points: Without understanding, your own or borrowed, you cannot live well. Many do not know what they do not know, and so never go looking for it. Asking for advice is not weakness; it shows sound judgment. For Nour: for areas outside your depth, such as tax, legal questions or a rare transmission fault, find the real expert and ask early rather than guessing and paying for it later.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 176 'Have Knowledge, or know those that have Knowledge' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Avoid Familiarities in Intercourse (maxim 177). Key points: Gracian warns that over-familiarity wears away respect: the more you expose, the more flaws show, and people may read friendliness as need. It is risky with superiors and unbecoming with subordinates. For Nour: be warm with the crew and customers, but keep a clear line between friendliness and favoritism, so decisions about schedules and pay stay fair and are seen to be fair.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 177 'Avoid Familiarities in Intercourse' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Trust your Heart (maxim 178). Key points: Especially once it has proved reliable, never refuse your instinct a hearing; it often warns of trouble before reasoning catches up. Fearing it without offering a better guide is useless. For Nour: if something about a deal or a hire still feels wrong after the numbers check out, pause and find what your gut has noticed before you sign.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 178 'Trust your Heart' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Reticence is the Seal of Capacity (maxim 179). Key points: A heart with no secrets is an open letter. Keeping confidences takes depth and self-control, and you pay a price to each person you tell. People will probe with questions, contradiction and irony to draw secrets out. For Nour: keep plans, numbers and crew matters inside the circle that needs them, but never keep a secret from a customer about their own car.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 179 'Reticence is the Seal of Capacity' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Never guide the Enemy to what he has to do (maxim 180). Key points: A fool will not follow the sensible path, and a shrewd opponent will not follow a plan you have laid out for them. Turn every question over from both sides, and while undecided, weigh what is possible more than what is probable. For Nour: do not announce the shop's next move in detail before it is ready; a competitor can copy a plan faster than a result.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 180 'Never guide the Enemy to what he has to do' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: The Truth, but not the whole Truth (maxim 181). Key points: Truth calls for great care, and telling it takes as much skill as keeping it. One lie wrecks a reputation for integrity, yet not every truth needs speaking, some for your own sake and some for others'. For Nour: never lie to a customer, and tell them everything that bears on their car and their money; discretion governs only how you say it and which crew matters stay private.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 181 'The Truth, but not the whole Truth' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: A Grain of Boldness in Everything (maxim 182). Key points: Do not rate others so highly that you fear them; up close, impressive people turn out human, with weaknesses of head or heart, and high office often outruns the person in it. Imagination paints things grander than they are. Wisdom should not be timid, nor folly rash. For Nour: walk into a meeting with a big vendor or a city office as an equal; they need good customers as much as the shop needs them.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 182 'A Grain of Boldness in Everything' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Do not hold your Views too firmly (maxim 183). Key points: Fools are the most certain, and the more wrong a view is, the tighter it gets held. Even when you are right, yielding gracefully often wins more than a stubborn victory. Firmness belongs to the will, not the mind. For Nour: be fixed on the goal, an honest shop that runs well, and flexible on method; if the data Nick shows you contradicts your hunch about a process, change your mind.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 183 'Do not hold your Views too firmly' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Do not be Ceremonious (maxim 184). Key points: Fussing over formality makes you tiresome and shows how fragile you think your dignity is. Expect respect, but do not become a master of ceremony; neither fake nor scorn etiquette, since no one is great by being great at small rituals. For Nour: skip process theater at the shop; a quick word with the crew at the start of the day beats a formal meeting no one needs.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 184 'Do not be Ceremonious' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Never stake your Credit on a single Cast (maxim 185). Key points: If everything rides on one attempt and it fails, the damage cannot be undone, and first tries often fail through bad timing. Link a second attempt to the first so one can redeem the other, and bring better means and more resources each time. For Nour: do not bet the shop's name on one big launch day; plan a sequence of smaller pushes so the second can correct the first.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 185 'Never stake your Credit on a single Cast' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Recognise Faults, whoever high placed (maxim 186). Key points: Integrity sees vice for what it is even when it wears silk or a crown. Great people may have great faults, but they are not great because of them, and flatterers excuse in the powerful what they would condemn in anyone else. For Nour: hold big vendors, platforms and yourself to the same standard you hold a new hire; a bad practice is not acceptable because a large company does it.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 186 'Recognise Faults, whoever high placed' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Do pleasant Things Yourself, unpleasant Things through Others (maxim 187). Key points: Gracian advises leaders to grant favors personally and route punishments through others, so goodwill attaches to them and resentment lands elsewhere. For Nour: keep the first half and reject the second; hand out praise yourself, and deliver hard news yourself too. Asking Mash or Manny to carry your unpopular calls spends their standing with the crew to protect yours.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 187 'Do pleasant Things Yourself, unpleasant Things through Others' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Be the Bearer of Praise (maxim 188). Key points: Speaking well of what is excellent shows good taste, gives others something to imitate, and quietly honors the people present. Belittling the absent to flatter the room is a cheap trick, and anyone who runs everyone down to everyone else cannot be trusted. For Nour: tell the crew when a customer praised their work by name, and never win a customer over by knocking another shop.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 188 'Be the Bearer of Praise' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Utilise Another's Wants (maxim 189). Key points: Gracian observes that the greater someone's need, the more leverage you hold, and that the skilled keep desire alive while preserving the other person's dependence. For Nour: refuse this with customers; a driver stuck with a flat is never an opening to squeeze. Earn repeat business by being the shop they would pick even with other options, and say plainly when a repair can safely wait.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 189 'Utilise Another's Wants' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Find Consolation in all Things (maxim 190). Key points: Every trouble carries some compensation. Gracian notes wryly that fortune seems to even things out, granting long life to the unimportant and heavy burdens to those who matter. For Nour: when an overloaded week sends more broken cars than the bay can handle, the consolation is real: the demand is there, and the strain shows exactly which process to fix next.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 190 'Find Consolation in all Things' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Do not take Payment in Politeness (maxim 191). Key points: Flattering words and lavish promises are counterfeit pay, and promising everything amounts to promising nothing. Real courtesy is doing what is owed; showy respect is usually aimed at your resources, not at you. For Nour: a vendor who is charming but late on deliveries has paid you in compliments; judge them by the delivery record, and hold the shop to the same rule: do what was promised.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 191 'Do not take Payment in Politeness' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Peaceful Life, a long Life (maxim 192). Key points: Live and let live: peacemakers run their own lives. Listen, observe and stay quiet; a day without quarrels brings untroubled sleep. Do not take everything to heart, but do take to heart what truly concerns you. For Nour: let small slights from callers or online strangers pass unanswered, so your energy and your sleep go to what actually matters, the shop and the people in it.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 192 'Peaceful Life, a long Life' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Watch him that begins with Another's to end with his own (maxim 193). Key points: Vigilance is the only defense against cunning, so pay attention to people's real intentions. Many get others to carry their business for them, and if you miss the motive you end up doing their risky work and getting burned for it. For Nour: when someone pitches a partnership framed as a favor to the shop, ask who carries the risk and who keeps the upside before agreeing.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 193 'Watch him that begins with Another's to end with his own' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Have reasonable Views of Yourself and of your Affairs (maxim 194). Key points: Everyone overrates themselves, the least deserving most of all, and hope makes promises experience does not keep. Hope for the best but expect the worst, so you meet whatever comes calmly; aim high, but not so high you miss from the start. For Nour: when sizing a NOUR OS build, plan the realistic version first and treat the ambitious one as a bonus, not the deadline.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 194 'Have reasonable Views of Yourself and of your Affairs' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Know how to Appreciate (maxim 195). Key points: Everyone can teach someone something, and no one is so excellent that they cannot be surpassed. The wise value everyone, spotting each person's strengths and respecting how hard anything good is to make; fools dismiss everyone. For Nour: the newest person in the shop may know a faster way to handle intake than anyone senior; ask them, and let the best method win regardless of seniority.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 195 'Know how to Appreciate' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Know your ruling Star (maxim 196). Key points: Everyone has some field where luck and fit favor them; the unlucky often simply have not found it. Equal ability succeeds in one place, role or crowd and not in another. Know where your luck runs as well as your talents, and follow it without mistaking someone else's path for yours. For Nour: notice which kinds of work and customers the shop wins naturally, and lean into those instead of chasing every segment.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 196 'Know your ruling Star' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Do not carry Fools on your Back (maxim 197). Key points: Failing to recognize a fool makes you one, and recognizing them while staying close is worse. They are risky company and dangerous confidants, and their stored-up folly eventually comes out; their one use to the wise is as a warning sign. For Nour: if a partner or vendor keeps making careless errors that land on your customers, end the arrangement, because their mistakes become the shop's reputation.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 197 'Do not carry Fools on your Back' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Know how to transplant Yourself (maxim 198). Key points: At home, talent is often undervalued: people remember your small beginnings, while anything from afar seems finished and impressive. Some who were laughed at in their village are honored elsewhere. For Nour: what the shop or NOUR OS does well may be valued more by people outside the neighborhood than by those who watched it start; do not let local familiarity set your sense of its worth.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 198 'Know how to transplant Yourself' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: To find a proper Place by Merit, not by Presumption (maxim 199). Key points: Merit is the true road to respect, and hard work shortens it. Merit alone can be overlooked, but pushing and demanding drags your reputation through the dust; the right way lies between deserving a place and pressing for it. For Nour: when seeking a bigger supplier account or a local partnership, lead with the shop's track record, ask once clearly, and do not badger.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 199 'To find a proper Place by Merit, not by Presumption' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Leave Something to wish for (maxim 200). Key points: When nothing is left to want, happiness sours into restlessness and fear, so keep some curiosity and hope alive, even in what you know. Gracian also advises never satisfying someone completely, so they keep needing you. For Nour: keep the first idea, always having a next goal for the shop, and reject the second; finish every customer's job completely and earn the return visit honestly.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 200 'Leave Something to wish for' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: They are all Fools who seem so besides half the rest (maxim 201). Key points: Foolishness is everywhere, and the worst case is the person sure that only others suffer from it. Wisdom starts with suspecting your own blind spots instead of cataloguing everyone else's. For Nour: when a week goes sideways, he checks his own calls first, the estimate he rushed or the instruction he never wrote down, before deciding the crew dropped the ball.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 201 'They are all Fools who seem so besides half the rest' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Words and Deeds make the Perfect Man (maxim 202). Key points: Speaking well matters, but acting well matters more: talk is easy and fades, while deeds last and carry the real weight of a life. Good action grows out of good thinking. For Nour: a feature in NOUR OS counts when it runs in production and changes his day, not when the plan for it reads well in a document.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 202 'Words and Deeds make the Perfect Man' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Know the great Men of your Age (maxim 203). Key points: Truly outstanding people are rare in any field, while the merely average are everywhere, and a grand title is empty without great work behind it. Learn to recognize the few who are the real thing. For Nour: when choosing whose playbook to study for the shop or for software, he picks operators with a proven record of results, not the loudest voice in his feed.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 203 'Know the great Men of your Age' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Attempt easy Tasks as if they were difficult, and difficult as if they were easy (maxim 204). Key points: Treat small jobs with care so confidence does not slide into carelessness, and treat big jobs as doable so fear does not freeze you. A task assumed finished is the one that stays undone, while steady effort wears down what looks impossible. For Nour: a routine tire swap gets the same careful finish as a hard diagnosis, and a large NOUR OS rebuild gets cut down to today's first small step.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 204 'Attempt easy Tasks as if they were difficult, and difficult as if they were easy' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Know how to play the Card of Contempt (maxim 205). Key points: Things chased too hard often slip away, and people who attack you to gain attention are best answered with silence, since a public rebuttal hands them the spotlight and marks your own name. Ignoring worthless critics is often the strongest reply. For Nour: when a rival or an online troll takes a swipe, he skips the public fight, keeps doing good work, and lets the shop's record answer.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 205 'Know how to play the Card of Contempt' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Know that there are vulgar Natures everywhere (maxim 206). Key points: Small-minded people turn up in every class and family, and a worse kind loudly sneers at the crowd while sharing all its faults. Learn to recognize that pattern so you can steer clear of it, in others and in yourself. For Nour: a customer who mocks every other shop in town will likely mock his too; he listens politely, stays professional, and does not pick up the tone.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 206 'Know that there are vulgar Natures everywhere' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Be Moderate (maxim 207). Key points: Passion makes judgment slip, and a single moment of anger or pleasure can undo years of careful conduct. Others may test you exactly in those heated moments, so restraint is your defense, and a careless remark can weigh heavily on whoever hears it. For Nour: when a customer pushes hard at the counter over a bill, he answers slowly and calmly, because words said in heat get repeated long after the car leaves.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 207 'Be Moderate' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Do not die of the Fools' Disease (maxim 208). Key points: Gracián plays with a paradox: some ruin themselves by thinking and feeling too much, others get by only because they think too little, and both are a kind of folly. Wisdom means knowing enough to act without drowning in worry. For Nour: on a late night of second-guessing a shop decision, he writes down the real risk, picks the next step, and stops replaying it.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 208 'Do not die of the Fools' Disease' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Keep Yourself free from common Follies (maxim 209). Key points: Shared follies are dangerous precisely because they are shared, so even sensible people fall into them: thinking your own lot is the worst, envying others, praising the past, prizing whatever is far away. Avoiding the crowd's errors takes deliberate attention. For Nour: he does not assume the shop down the road or a startup online has it easier; he judges his own numbers on their own terms.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 209 'Keep Yourself free from common Follies' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Know how to play the Card of Truth (maxim 210). Key points: A good person must tell the truth even when it is risky, and the skill lies in the delivery, because breaking someone's illusion is bitter. A careful manner lets the same truth help rather than wound. For Nour: when a car needs more work than the customer hoped, he tells them plainly and completely, with care in how he says it, and never softens the facts themselves.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 210 'Know how to play the Card of Truth' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: In Heaven all is bliss (maxim 211). Key points: Life on earth mixes good and bad fortune, and no stretch of it is all luck or all trouble. The wise stay steady through the swings, expect complications, and steer so the story ends well. For Nour: a slow week at the shop and a packed one are both normal weather; he keeps the same routine through both and plays for the long run.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 211 'In Heaven all is bliss' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Keep to Yourself the final Touches of your Art (maxim 212). Key points: Old masters held back the last refinements of their craft so pupils stayed dependent and the teacher stayed on top, and Gracián prizes that reserve as a rule for success. For Nour: the honest version is to keep raising his own standard so he always has more to teach, while training Zach and the rest of the crew fully; the shop is stronger when skill is shared, not hoarded.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 212 'Keep to Yourself the final Touches of your Art' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Know how to Contradict (maxim 213). Key points: Gracián notes that mild doubt draws people out: when challenged, they explain more and reveal what they would otherwise keep hidden, and a student who pushes back gets a fuller lesson. For Nour: he uses honest pushback, never feigned doubt, asking a vendor or a tech why and then why again to reach the real reasoning behind a recommendation, and he never uses it to trip up a customer.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 213 'Know how to Contradict' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Do not turn one Blunder into two (maxim 214). Key points: One mistake often breeds several more when people scramble to cover it, just as one lie needs others to prop it up. A wise person may slip once but does not compound it. For Nour: if the shop gets an order wrong, he owns it with the customer right away and fixes it, instead of explaining it away and creating a second problem on top of the first.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 214 'Do not turn one Blunder into two' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Watch him that acts on Second Thoughts (maxim 215). Key points: Some people hide what they want, act indifferent or let you win small points, then turn and go straight for their real aim. Stay alert, notice the pretext, and at times let them see that you understand the play. For Nour: when a vendor opens with a sweet first deal, he reads the terms that follow it before committing, and asks plainly what they want from the relationship.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 215 'Watch him that acts on Second Thoughts' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Be Expressive (maxim 216). Key points: Good ideas are not enough; they must come out clearly, and many people have rich thoughts that emerge muddled. Murky talk sometimes earns a kind of respect, but no listener can follow someone who attaches no clear meaning to his words. For Nour: when he briefs an AI session or the crew, one clear sentence of what done looks like beats a long, foggy message.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 216 'Be Expressive' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Neither Love nor Hate, for ever (maxim 217). Key points: Friendships can turn, so do not hand anyone weapons they could later use against you; enmities can end, so always leave room for reconciliation. Old grudges tend to come back as present regrets. For Nour: he keeps sensitive shop details out of casual friendships, and he leaves the door open with a supplier or contact he once fell out with.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 217 'Neither Love nor Hate, for ever' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Never act from Obstinacy but from Knowledge (maxim 218). Key points: Stubbornness is passion dressed up as principle; people who must win every exchange turn allies into enemies and end up with nothing but trouble. Decide from what you know, not from the need to be right. For Nour: if Mash or Manny shows him a better way to run the morning rush, he switches without turning it into a contest.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 218 'Never act from Obstinacy but from Knowledge' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Do not pass for a Hypocrite (maxim 219). Key points: Be known as prudent rather than cunning: sincerity wins people, though it should not turn naive, and shrewdness should not slide into trickery. Better to be respected as wise than feared as sly. For Nour: the shop's reputation should be that it says what it means, so the counter never quotes one thing and invoices another.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 219 'Do not pass for a Hypocrite' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: If you cannot clothe Yourself in Lion's skin use Foxpelt (maxim 220). Key points: When force will not win, use cleverness; skill has achieved more than strength, and adapting to the times can mean leading them. Gracián allows the side road of cunning when the main road is blocked. For Nour: when a bigger chain outspends him, he wins with smarter moves such as faster answers and better follow-up, never with tricks that mislead a customer.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 220 'If you cannot clothe Yourself in Lion's skin use Foxpelt' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Do not seize Occasions to embarrass Yourself or Others (maxim 221). Key points: Some people are walking stumbling blocks, always contradicting, finding fault and turning small irritations into constant friction. They are easy to run into and hard to shake off, and they test everyone's patience. For Nour: he watches that he never becomes that person in the bay, correcting every small thing out loud; he saves corrections for what matters and makes them privately.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 221 'Do not seize Occasions to embarrass Yourself or Others' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Reserve is proof of Prudence (maxim 222). Key points: Once the tongue runs loose it is hard to rein in, and the way someone talks reveals the state of his mind to anyone paying attention. The wise speak carefully, sparing themselves trouble and showing self-command. For Nour: he keeps plans that are not yet decided out of shop chatter, so the crew is not chasing rumors about changes that may never happen.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 222 'Reserve is proof of Prudence' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Be not Eccentric (maxim 223). Key points: Odd habits, whether put on for show or simply careless, usually read as flaws rather than distinction, and they brand a person in a way that invites mockery or dislike. For Nour: the shop's look and voice should stay clean and consistent, so customers remember the work and the honesty rather than a gimmick.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 223 'Be not Eccentric' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Never take Things against the Grain (maxim 224). Key points: Everything has a smooth side and a rough side: a blade grabbed the wrong way cuts, while an enemy's spear held by the shaft can protect you. The skill is finding the useful angle in whatever happens. For Nour: a bad review or a lost customer is also free information about what to fix, so he reads it for that, not only for the sting.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 224 'Never take Things against the Grain' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Know your chief Fault (maxim 225). Key points: Everyone carries a weakness right beside their greatest strength, and if desire feeds it, it can take over. Name it openly, fight it with prudence, and lesser faults tend to fall with it, because self-mastery starts with self-knowledge. For Nour: he names the one habit of his that most often costs the shop, and invites Mash and Manny to flag it when they see it happen.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 225 'Know your chief Fault' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Take care to be Obliging (maxim 226). Key points: People act less from who they are than from what they feel they owe, and being right is not enough without goodwill behind it. Small kindnesses cost little and return a lot, and a connection that seems useless today may be needed someday. For Nour: a minute of honest advice for a walk-in who is not buying today costs almost nothing and can bring that driver back later.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 226 'Take care to be Obliging' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Do not be the Slave of First Impressions (maxim 227). Key points: Some people lock onto the first story they hear and treat every later version as an intruder, which lets the quickest liar win. Keep an ear for the other side and wait for the second or third report before deciding. For Nour: when a customer complains about a job, he hears from Zach or whoever did the work and checks the invoice notes before judging.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 227 'Do not be the Slave of First Impressions' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Do not be a Scandal-monger (maxim 228). Key points: Mocking others is easy and makes you disliked, and everyone you mock has friends who will answer for them. Ill will should never be your amusement or your topic. For Nour: no trash talk about other shops or about customers at the counter or in group texts; the crew takes its tone from the one he sets.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 228 'Do not be a Scandal-monger' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Plan out your Life wisely (maxim 229). Key points: Live by design rather than chance, and mix enjoyment into the trip so it does not grind. Gracián sketches three stages: learn from books and the dead, then from living people and the wider world, then give time to yourself and reflection. For Nour: he can set regular time to read the best operators, time to learn from other businesses, and protected time to think about where the shop is going.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 229 'Plan out your Life wisely' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Open your Eyes betimes (maxim 230). Key points: Seeing too late is often worse than not seeing; some only wake up after they have wrecked things, and the people around them may profit from keeping them blind. A blind rider never keeps a healthy horse. For Nour: he reads the shop's numbers every week, not only when something feels off, and stays wary of anyone who benefits from him not looking.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 230 'Open your Eyes betimes' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Never let Things be seen half-finished (maxim 231). Key points: Work in progress looks rough, and that first sight sticks and spoils the finished result. Show the work when it is whole. For Nour: a car goes back to its owner clean and fully buttoned up, and a new NOUR OS screen ships when it works end to end, not as a half-wired demo he has to explain away.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 231 'Never let Things be seen half-finished' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Have a Touch of the Trader (maxim 232). Key points: Too much reflection and too little action leaves even brilliant people easy to fool, because they know rare things but miss ordinary ones. Keep enough practical, street-level sense that nobody can cheat you. For Nour: he knows his parts costs, labor times and supplier terms cold, so no vendor and no software pitch can talk past him.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 232 'Have a Touch of the Trader' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Let not the proffered Morsel be distasteful (maxim 233). Key points: A favor offered without regard for the other person's taste can insult instead of please, since what flatters one person offends another. Learn what someone values before you try to help them. For Nour: some customers want the full technical walkthrough and others want a short answer and their keys; he asks which they prefer instead of giving everyone the same speech.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 233 'Let not the proffered Morsel be distasteful' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Never trust your Honour to another, unless you have his in Pledge (maxim 234). Key points: When your reputation depends on someone else's discretion, Gracián advises arranging things so their interest is tied to yours and any disclosure would hurt both sides. For Nour: the clean version is written agreements and shared stakes, so a partner or vendor has real reasons to keep commitments, rather than two people holding secrets over each other.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 234 'Never trust your Honour to another, unless you have his in Pledge' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Know how to Ask (maxim 235). Key points: Some people cannot refuse anything, while others start every answer with no, and those call for tact and good timing. Ask when they are in a good mood, not right after someone else was turned down or after bad news. For Nour: he brings a big request to a supplier rep after a smooth delivery, not the day after a dispute, and makes the ask clear and specific.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 235 'Know how to Ask' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Make an Obligation beforehand of what would have to be a Reward afterwards (maxim 236). Key points: Grant favors before they are earned: given early, the gift binds the person more, and what would later be a mere reward becomes a debt of goodwill. It only works with people who feel gratitude; with others it slows them down. For Nour: backing a promising crew member with training before it is owed can build loyalty, but only with people who answer trust with effort, and never as a hidden hook.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 236 'Make an Obligation beforehand of what would have to be a Reward afterwards' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Never share the Secrets of your Superiors (maxim 237). Key points: Being a powerful person's confidant is risky: they later resent whoever saw them at their weakest, and the secret makes the holder a threat. Gracián's rule is to neither tell secrets nor ask to hear them. For Nour: he keeps the shop's sensitive matters on a need-to-know basis instead of loading a crew member with them, and he does not pry into a vendor's internal troubles.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 237 'Never share the Secrets of your Superiors' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Know what is wanting in Yourself (maxim 238). Key points: Many capable people fall short of greatness because of one missing quality, such as warmth, organizing ability or moderation. Spot the gap and practice the missing habit until it becomes second nature. For Nour: if one capability is missing from how the shop runs, for example a written routine for a recurring task, he names it and either builds the habit himself or hands it to whoever is strongest there.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 238 'Know what is wanting in Yourself' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Do not be Captious (maxim 239). Key points: Being sensible beats being nitpicky; knowing more than the moment needs can dull your edge, since very fine points bend or snap. Long debates over details breed quarrels, while plain common sense stays on the actual task. For Nour: when a code review or a debate over an estimate turns into hair-splitting, he steers back to the one question that decides it.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 239 'Do not be Captious' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Make use of Folly (maxim 240). Key points: Gracián says the wise sometimes act less clever than they are and speak each person's language, because showing off brains can cost goodwill. The real fool is the one who lacks sense, not the one who chooses to look simple. For Nour: he explains a repair in plain words without jargon, meeting customers where they are, but he never plays dumb to dodge a fair question.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 240 'Make use of Folly' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Put up with Raillery, but do not practise it (maxim 241). Key points: Taking a joke well is a courtesy and a sign of strength, while dishing out mockery can backfire, since serious quarrels have grown out of jokes. Before teasing anyone, know how much they can take. For Nour: he laughs off the crew's ribbing but is careful with his own jabs, especially toward newer people who cannot easily push back on the owner.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 241 'Put up with Raillery, but do not practise it' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Push Advantages (maxim 242). Key points: Many pour all their energy into the start and never finish; they invent but do not execute, or they clear the obstacle and stop short of the win. If a project is worth starting it is worth finishing, and if not, it should never have started. For Nour: open pull requests and half-done shop projects get closed out before new ones begin, so effort turns into results instead of a pile of starts.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 242 'Push Advantages' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Do not be too much of a Dove (maxim 243). Key points: Honest people are the easiest to fool, because those who never lie expect others not to. Pair innocence with the serpent's alertness, using as much caution as schemers use traps. For Nour: he stays straight with every customer and still verifies a too-good supplier offer, an unusual payment request or a sudden urgent email before acting on it.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 243 'Do not be too much of a Dove' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Create a feeling of Obligation (maxim 244). Key points: Some people turn favors they receive into favors they seem to grant, asking and praising so gracefully that you end up feeling indebted to them. Gracián admires the trick and admires spotting it even more. For Nour: he notices when a vendor or contact flips the ledger this way and settles fairly, while he himself thanks people plainly for what they do for him instead of spinning it.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 244 'Create a feeling of Obligation' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Original and out-of-the-way Views (maxim 245). Key points: Someone who never disagrees with you is pleasing himself, not serving you, and flattery always sends a bill. Criticism from the wrong people can be a credit, and work that pleases everyone may be ordinary. For Nour: he keeps people and AI tools around him that say when an idea is weak, and he worries more about universal nodding than about pushback.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 245 'Original and out-of-the-way Views' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Never offer Satisfaction unless it is demanded (maxim 246). Key points: Apologizing or explaining before anyone asks plants suspicion that was not there; an early excuse reads like a confession. Let clean conduct answer distrust. For Nour: honesty comes first, so he tells a customer anything they need to know without being asked; but he does not pile nervous justifications onto a fair invoice, and lets clear line items speak for themselves.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 246 'Never offer Satisfaction unless it is demanded' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Know a little more, live a little less (maxim 247). Key points: Time is the only thing truly yours, so do not waste it on mechanical chores or bury yourself in a heap of important work. Piling up occupations breeds envy and exhausts the mind, though learning itself is part of really living. For Nour: he hands repetitive tasks to the crew or to NOUR OS automation and keeps his own hours for learning and judgment calls.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 247 'Know a little more, live a little less' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Do not go with the last speaker (maxim 248). Key points: Some people take the shape of whoever spoke to them last, like soft wax, losing every earlier view; they are unstable and useless as advisers. Hold a position until a real reason moves it. For Nour: a plan agreed with Mash in the morning does not flip because a salesperson called in the afternoon; any change needs a reason he can state out loud.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 248 'Do not go with the last speaker' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Never begin Life with what should end it (maxim 249). Key points: Many take their leisure first and push the hard work to the end, or chase trivial learning before the studies that matter. Put the essentials first and the extras after, if room remains, because method governs both knowledge and life. For Nour: each day the work that brings in cars and keeps promises comes first, and nice-to-have NOUR OS features wait until that is handled.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 249 'Never begin Life with what should end it' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: When to change the Conversation (maxim 250). Key points: With some people everything runs backward: they run down what they secretly want and praise the bad to avoid praising the good. When talk turns malicious, read it in reverse or move it somewhere else. For Nour: a buyer who knocks the value of used equipment he wants from the shop may simply want it cheaper; he notes that and keeps the talk on facts.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 250 'When to change the Conversation' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Use human Means as if there were no divine ones, and divine as if there were no human ones (maxim 251). Key points: Gracián calls this a master rule that needs no comment: work as though everything depends on your own effort, and trust as though everything depends on what is beyond you. Full effort and calm acceptance belong together. For Nour: he prepares the shop as if every outcome rests on preparation, then meets the slow days and lucky breaks he cannot control without panic.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 251 'Use human Means as if there were no divine ones, and divine as if there were no human ones' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Neither belong entirely to Yourself nor entirely to Others (maxim 252). Key points: Living only for yourself is selfish and leaves you unsupported when luck fails, while living only for others leaves you no hour of your own. Belong to others enough that they belong to you, and remember people often seek what you can do for them. For Nour: he stays reachable to the crew in the rush, but blocks time each week that no request can take.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 252 'Neither belong entirely to Yourself nor entirely to Others' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Do not Explain overmuch (maxim 253). Key points: Gracián observes that people undervalue what they fully grasp and admire what seems slightly beyond them, so he advises against spelling out everything. For Nour: with customers the honest rule wins, explaining every repair and every charge clearly; the restraint belongs in not drowning people in detail they did not ask for, and in not narrating plans that are still unfinished.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 253 'Do not Explain overmuch' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Never despise an Evil, however small (maxim 254). Key points: Troubles rarely arrive alone; one slip can pull others after it until no one can tell where the losses will stop. Do not shrug off a small problem, and do not stir up trouble that is lying quiet. For Nour: a recurring small glitch in NOUR OS or a comeback on a single job gets traced to its cause right away, before it gathers company.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 254 'Never despise an Evil, however small' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Do Good a little at a time, but often (maxim 255). Key points: Give in amounts the other person can repay; a huge favor feels like a debt, and people sometimes walk away rather than stay forever owing you. Small, regular kindnesses that cost little but are truly wanted go further. For Nour: steady small gestures toward the crew, such as giving credit for good work in front of others, build more loyalty than one big gesture nobody can match.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 255 'Do Good a little at a time, but often' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Go armed against Discourtesy (maxim 256). Key points: Rudeness, bad faith and foolishness are common, so prepare each day to meet them calmly and keep your reputation out of cheap clashes; a tactful sidestep often works better than a fight. For Nour: he and the crew can agree in advance how to handle an angry customer at the counter; Gracián suggests feigning misunderstanding, but the honest sidestep is to restate the facts calmly and politely.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 256 'Go armed against Discourtesy' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Never let Matters come to a Rupture (maxim 257). Key points: An open break always damages your reputation, and almost anyone can hurt you even if few can help. If a split cannot be avoided, let it look like a gradual cooling rather than an explosion. For Nour: when a supplier relationship has to end, he ends it politely and in writing, without a shouting match that others will retell for years.
