entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 257 'Never let Matters come to a Rupture' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Find out some one to share your Troubles (maxim 258). Key points: Standing alone means carrying all the blame when things go wrong; Gracián notes, wryly, that a doctor who failed calls a consultation so someone shares the burden. Weight is lighter when shared. For Nour: on big calls he brings Mash and Manny in early so the decision is honestly shared from the start, not so he has someone to blame if it fails.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 258 'Find out some one to share your Troubles' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Anticipate Injuries and turn them into Favours (maxim 259). Key points: It is wiser to head off harm than to avenge it, and the rarest skill is turning a rival into a confidant. Fill the space with goodwill and there is little room left for injury. For Nour: a nearby shop that sees him as a rival might become a referral partner for work neither handles well alone, if he reaches out first.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 259 'Anticipate Injuries and turn them into Favours' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: We belong to none and none to us, entirely (maxim 260). Key points: No bond, not family and not the closest friendship, means telling everything; even intimates keep something back, and full confidence is different from full regard. Each relationship gets its own share of openness. For Nour: different people see different parts of the picture, the crew the operational side and an adviser the books, and that is fine as long as nobody is misled.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 260 'We belong to none and none to us, entirely' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Do not follow up a Folly (maxim 261). Key points: Many treat a wrong turn as a commitment and keep going to look consistent, regretting it inside while defending it outside. A hasty promise or a mistaken resolution does not truly bind you. For Nour: if a new process or tool is not working after a fair trial, he stops it and says so, rather than defending it for weeks to save face.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 261 'Do not follow up a Folly' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Be able to Forget (maxim 262). Key points: Memory clings to what we would rather drop and loses what we want to keep; often the only cure for an injury is to let it go. Train memory with good habits, since it can make life pleasant or miserable. For Nour: after a bad day at the shop, he reviews what to fix once, writes it down, and then lets the sting go instead of replaying it.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 262 'Be able to Forget' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Many things of Taste one should not possess oneself (maxim 263). Key points: Things you only enjoy now and then are often better borrowed than owned; the owner enjoys them for a day, then carries the upkeep and the hassle of lending. Ownership can bring more trouble than pleasure. For Nour: before buying equipment or software the shop would use only occasionally, he weighs renting or paying for a service, since owning brings maintenance and storage too.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 263 'Many things of Taste one should not possess oneself' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Have no careless Days (maxim 264). Key points: Fortune likes to catch people off guard, so readiness has to be constant, and the day you relax is often the day you are tested. A shrewd examiner skips the parade day and picks the unexpected one. For Nour: the shop runs every day as if the most demanding customer is about to walk in, because with walk-ins seven days a week, any day can be that day.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 264 'Have no careless Days' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Set those under you difficult Tasks (maxim 265). Key points: Many people discover their own ability only when a hard challenge forces it out, the way fear of drowning turns someone into a swimmer. A good leader hands people stretching work and so creates capable people. For Nour: giving Zach a harder diagnostic job, with backup nearby, may show him and the rest of the crew what he can really do.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 265 'Set those under you difficult Tasks' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Do not become Bad from sheer Goodness (maxim 266). Key points: Someone who never gets angry, whether from mildness or plain inability, is not admirable; people simply stop taking him seriously. Showing strong feeling when it is warranted is part of character, and good taste mixes bitter with sweet. For Nour: being easygoing with the crew should not mean letting a repeated safety shortcut slide; when something matters, he lets them see that it matters.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 266 'Do not become Bad from sheer Goodness' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Silken Words, sugared Manners (maxim 267). Key points: Harsh words wound deeper than blows, and pleasant speech achieves a great deal at little cost; Gracián even calls it an art to sell air. Keep your speech gracious so even opponents find it agreeable. For Nour: a warm, polite tone at the counter costs nothing, but kind words must carry true content, and he never uses smooth talk to cover a fact the customer needs.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 267 'Silken Words, sugared Manners' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: The Wise do at once what the Fool does at last (maxim 268). Key points: The wise and the foolish often end up doing the same thing; the difference is timing. The wise see early what must be done eventually and do it willingly, earning credit, while the fool is dragged into it late. For Nour: a fix he knows the shop will need, like replacing a weak process or system, is cheaper and calmer done now than after it breaks in a rush.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 268 'The Wise do at once what the Fool does at last' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Make use of the Novelty of your Position (maxim 269). Key points: People prize what is new, and a fresh face can outrank long-familiar excellence, but that shine fades within days. Use the early window of attention well, because it closes fast. For Nour: when the shop launches something new, such as a new page or a NOUR OS feature, he puts the effort into the first weeks of attention and has the follow-up ready before launch.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 269 'Make use of the Novelty of your Position' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Do not condemn alone that which pleases all (maxim 270). Key points: If many people enjoy something, there is probably something good in it even if you cannot name it, and standing alone against it mostly damages your own credibility. If you cannot see the merit, keep quiet rather than condemn. For Nour: before dismissing a tool, platform or practice that many well-run shops use, he works out what they are getting from it.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 270 'Do not condemn alone that which pleases all' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: In every Occupation if you know little stick to the safest (maxim 271). Key points: When you lack expertise, take the proven route; you may not look brilliant, but you will be seen as reliable. Only the well trained can improvise safely, and chasing risk with little knowledge invites ruin. For Nour: on an unfamiliar repair or an unfamiliar kind of software change, the shop follows the documented procedure or calls in someone who knows, rather than improvising.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 271 'In every Occupation if you know little stick to the safest' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Sell Things by the Tariff of Courtesy (maxim 272). Key points: Courtesy binds people more than any bargain; a decent person feels a generous gesture as a debt worth more than its price. Good manners add a second value to whatever you provide, though crude people miss it. For Nour: the price stays the price on the estimate, and the courtesy around it, a clear explanation and a respectful handoff, is what brings customers back.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 272 'Sell Things by the Tariff of Courtesy' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Comprehend their Dispositions with whom you deal (maxim 273). Key points: Know a person's temperament and you can anticipate what they intend: the gloomy expect disaster, gossips expect scandal, and strong feeling distorts what people report. Read the person behind the words. For Nour: an anxious customer and a skeptical one need different handling of the same estimate, and noticing which one he is facing helps him explain it in a way that person can hear.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 273 'Comprehend their Dispositions with whom you deal' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Be Attractive (maxim 274). Key points: Merit alone is not enough; it needs grace and a pleasant manner to win general goodwill, which is the most practical way to lead. Popularity is partly luck, but skill can cultivate it. For Nour: good workmanship plus a friendly greeting and easy communication make the shop the place people choose, not just a place that can do the job.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 274 'Be Attractive' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Join in the Game as far as Decency permits (maxim 275). Key points: Do not always stand on dignity and become a bore; joining in common fun wins goodwill, but never go so far that you embarrass yourself, since one careless day can cost what years of work built. For Nour: he can join the crew's banter and shop get-togethers, while keeping a line that protects his standing as the one who sets the standard.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 275 'Join in the Game as far as Decency permits' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Know how to renew your Character (maxim 276). Key points: People change over the years, so steer that change toward something better, adding a new strength at each stage, and expect growth in others as well. New roles often reshape how people behave. For Nour: each year he can pick one capability to add as an operator and builder, and give crew members room to grow into bigger roles as they mature.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 276 'Know how to renew your Character' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Display yourself (maxim 277). Key points: Talent needs to be shown at the right moment, and display gives real excellence a second life, but it must be timely, unforced and moderate or it turns into vanity. Reveal ability gradually so each success promises the next. For Nour: the shop shares real finished work and genuine customer outcomes, with permission, one at a time rather than in one big boast; display must rest on actual quality.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 277 'Display yourself' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Avoid Notoriety in all Things (maxim 278). Key points: Even good qualities turn into faults when they are flaunted, because standing out for its own sake draws blame, and some people even chase fame through outrageous conduct. For Nour: the shop should be known for steady, honest work, not for stunts or edgy marketing that grabs attention and spends trust.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 278 'Avoid Notoriety in all Things' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Do not contradict the Contradicter (maxim 279). Key points: When someone keeps contradicting you, work out whether it is honest stubbornness or a ploy to draw you out; the first is a nuisance, the second a danger. Keep your guard up so a probing argument does not pry loose what you meant to keep. For Nour: when a caller fishing for competitive details keeps arguing for specifics, he stays courteous and does not let the argument pull out internal information.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 279 'Do not contradict the Contradicter' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Be Trustworthy (maxim 280). Key points: Gracián complains that honest dealing has grown rare and promises are often broken, yet other people's bad conduct should serve as a warning, not a model. A person of honor does not forget who he is because of what others are. For Nour: if other shops overpromise or pad bills, that is the reason for his shop to be the one whose word and invoice hold up every time.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 280 'Be Trustworthy' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Find Favour with Men of Sense (maxim 281). Key points: A lukewarm yes from a truly discerning person outweighs a crowd's applause, which is smoke nobody can live on. Lasting approval comes from those who understand the work. For Nour: the respect of a sharp mechanic or a skilled engineer whose judgment he trusts counts for more than chasing likes, so he seeks feedback from people who know the craft.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 281 'Find Favour with Men of Sense' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Make use of Absence to make yourself more esteemed or valued (maxim 282). Key points: Familiarity wears down respect while absence lets imagination enlarge someone, so Gracián advises stepping back now and then to be valued more. For Nour: the honest use is to build a shop that runs well when he is not there, so stepping away shows the strength of the system and the crew, rather than staying scarce just to seem important.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 282 'Make use of Absence to make yourself more esteemed or valued' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Have the Gift of Discovery (maxim 283). Key points: Inventing something truly new is rare and marks real talent, while choosing the right means is the mark of sound sense. Novelty is risky in matters of judgment, where it drifts into paradox, but earns praise in creative work when it succeeds. For Nour: NOUR OS is the right place to try new ideas, while the shop's core judgments, like what a car actually needs, stay on proven ground.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 283 'Have the Gift of Discovery' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Do not be Importunate (maxim 284). Key points: Respect yourself and others will follow; be sparing with your presence and show up when wanted, so you are welcome. If you push into something uninvited, you carry the blame if it fails and get no thanks if it works. For Nour: follow-up with past customers should be useful and well spaced, never pushy, so a message from the shop is welcomed rather than ignored.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 284 'Do not be Importunate' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Never die of another's Ill-luck (maxim 285). Key points: People stuck in trouble often pull others in for company, and helping them takes care so you do not sink alongside them. Help, but keep your own footing. For Nour: he can support a struggling business contact or crew member with advice and fair treatment, without taking on their debts or risks in a way that puts the shop in danger.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 285 'Never die of another's Ill-luck' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Do not become responsible for all or for every one (maxim 286). Key points: Taking on everyone's burdens makes you everyone's servant, and freedom is worth more than the favors you would trade it for. Stay independent rather than making many depend on you, and watch for responsibility offered as a hook. For Nour: he builds the crew so decisions do not all route through him, and declines obligations handed to him mainly to make him dependent on someone.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 286 'Do not become responsible for all or for every one' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Never act in a Passion (maxim 287). Key points: Acting in anger ruins everything, because passion pushes reason out and you are no longer yourself. Bring in a calm go-between, since onlookers see the game more clearly, and step back the moment you feel your temper rising. For Nour: when a dispute heats up at the counter, he pauses or lets Manny or Mash take it for a moment, before saying anything he would regret.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 287 'Never act in a Passion' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Live for the Moment (maxim 288). Key points: Actions should fit the circumstances: act while the chance exists and do not bind yourself to rigid rules, except the core virtues. The option you reject today may be the one you need tomorrow. For Nour: shop plans flex with the day's walk-ins and conditions, but honesty with customers is one of the fixed rules that never bends.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 288 'Live for the Moment' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Nothing depreciates a Man more than to show he is a Man like other Men (maxim 289). Key points: Gracián warns that frivolity destroys respect faster than any other failing, since a person seen as lightweight cannot carry weight even in later years. For Nour: the useful part is avoiding careless, flippant conduct in front of customers and crew; being openly human, such as admitting a mistake or a limit, earns trust rather than costing it.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 289 'Nothing depreciates a Man more than to show he is a Man like other Men' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: 'Tis a piece of good Fortune to combine Men's Love and Respect (maxim 290). Key points: Affection and respect pull against each other: as familiarity grows, esteem tends to recede, so aim to be neither too feared nor too adored. Better to be loved with respect than loved with passion. For Nour: he can be warm with the crew and still keep the boundaries a leader needs, so friendliness never makes standards negotiable.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 290 ''Tis a piece of good Fortune to combine Men's Love and Respect' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Know how to Test (maxim 291). Key points: Guard against bad actors by judging people carefully; understanding character matters more than understanding materials. Words reveal integrity, and actions reveal it more. For Nour: a prospective hire can show what he does on a real job before full trust is given, and a new vendor can earn a bigger account by handling a small order well first.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 291 'Know how to Test' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Let your personal Qualities surpass those of your Office (maxim 292). Key points: The person should be bigger than the post: capable people grow as their role grows, while narrow people shrink and stumble under responsibility. Augustus cared more about being a great man than a great ruler. For Nour: as owner, his standing should rest on the judgment and character the crew sees every day, not on the title on the door.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 292 'Let your personal Qualities surpass those of your Office' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Maturity (maxim 293). Key points: Maturity shows in conduct more than in dress; it is a calm authority, not the numbness of a fool, and it finishes a person's ability and draws respect. A composed bearing presents the inner person well. For Nour: steady, unhurried responses during a chaotic weekend rush tell the crew and customers more than any speech could.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 293 'Maturity' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Be moderate in your Views (maxim 294). Key points: Everyone forms opinions in line with their interests, and two people can hold opposite views each sure of their reasons. Before judging, put yourself in the other person's place and examine why they think as they do. For Nour: when Mash and Manny disagree on how to handle a packed afternoon, he asks each to argue the other's case before he decides.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 294 'Be moderate in your Views' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Do not affect what you have not effected (maxim 295). Key points: Claiming deeds you did not do is contemptible vanity, and the more you have really done, the less you need to advertise it. Do the work, let others do the talking, and never pay for praise. For Nour: shop marketing claims only what the shop truly does, and he never buys fake reviews or lets anyone inflate a result.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 295 'Do not affect what you have not effected' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Noble Qualities (maxim 296). Key points: One great quality outweighs a crowd of middling ones, and just as some people want everything they own to be grand, a person should make the qualities of character as large as possible. Greatness should run through deeds and words alike. For Nour: rather than spreading thin across many small virtues, he can build a few large ones, like reliability and fairness, into every part of how the shop works.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 296 'Noble Qualities' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Always act as if your Acts were seen (maxim 297). Key points: Assume you are being watched, because walls have ears and sooner or later everything comes out. Behave alone exactly as you would in front of everyone. For Nour: work done where no customer can see, a hidden fastener or a part nobody will inspect, gets the same quality as work done in front of them, and the same goes for code nobody reviews.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 297 'Always act as if your Acts were seen' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Three Things go to a Prodigy (maxim 298). Key points: Gracián names three gifts that make an exceptional person: a fertile wit, a deep intellect and refined taste. Thinking well is good and thinking rightly is better, and some minds see most clearly in the dark while others find the fitting move under pressure. For Nour: he can build all three on purpose, generating options, testing them hard, and choosing with taste, especially when a shop situation is murky.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 298 'Three Things go to a Prodigy' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: Leave off Hungry (maxim 299). Key points: Stop while appetite remains: demand sets value, and too much of a good thing dulls it, while a little of something excellent is worth twice as much. For Nour: the shop's social posts and messages should be few and worth reading, leaving people looking forward to the next one rather than tuning out from overload.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 299 'Leave off Hungry' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation

entries.text: TL;DR: In one word, be a Saint (maxim 300). Key points: Virtue ties every good quality together and sits at the center of real happiness; it makes a person prudent, brave, trustworthy and truthful. Greatness is measured by character, not by fortune, and character is what people remember. For Nour: the shop and NOUR OS are both worth building only on that base, so integrity is the test he applies before profit, speed or cleverness.
entries.context: Gracián, Oráculo manual (1647), maxim 300 'In one word, be a Saint' · Jacobs 1892 translation (public domain) · distillation and application ours, not a quotation
